### WP0: Upstream integration and upstream reports

WP0 owns everything that crosses a repository boundary: the user's open glue and glue-qt PRs, PRs by others that later WPs build on, reports and requests to glue, glue-qt, irispy and astropy, and the register of temporary glue-solar workarounds that those fixes retire. Primary paths: `glue_solar/__init__.py` (gated patches), `pyproject.toml` (floors), `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/upstream/` (reproducers) and the three tables below. Every PR, issue or comment action needs the user's direction. New PRs suit generic fixes or features that belong in glue-core or glue-qt (as Qt #74/#75 did), and solar work never waits for them (D2, D5). What done means at each milestone:

- M0: the gating rule, the register, and drafted reports for the M0 blockers (Pixel crosshair, `translate_pixel`, large-data Cancel, `AggregateSlice`, the irispy flip/CRPIX/units/-TAB index bugs, astropy#19174).
- M1: the integrated stack validated; the restore-priority and session-saver PRs filed, with their gated workarounds; the irispy requests that other WPs cite filed; each release's contents recorded and floors raised.
- M2 and M3: tracking of the upstream work that WP7 and WP12 build on, plus optional proposals.

WP1 owns the real-IRIS autolink/coherence regression and WP5 the numeric/WCSAxes marker tests. WP0 only tracks their PRs.

The error is 0.168″ for full-resolution SJI, 0.47″ for rolled binned SJI and 0.607″ for AIA. SLTPX1IX uses the same convention, so report both together. ### WP1: Coordinates, units and links

WP1 gives IRIS data and glue-solar's own sunpy maps one coordinate contract towards glue: canonical helioprojective and wavelength names, arcsec and Angstrom (D3), and coherent low- and high-level WCS APIs. It also owns the link graph: the permanent, time-aware `link_hpc` world links (D1), the per-pair policy once core #2595 supplies APE-14 `WCSLink`s, and the combined-graph regression. Primary paths are `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py`, `glue_solar/sources/iris.py`, `glue_solar/sources/maps.py`, `glue_solar/sources/loaders/maps.py`, a new `glue_solar/glue_patches.py`, `glue_solar/tests/test_linking.py` and `glue_solar/tests/test_importer.py`. The prototype delta is ported onto `main`; the prototype package is never copied over it.

Done per milestone:
- **M0**, on released glue-core 1.27.0, glue-qt 0.4.2 and irispy-lmsal 0.9.0: the browser and a menu action install `link_hpc`, SJI world coordinates match the header WCS at the sampled frames, datasets share axis names, and the link-graph regression passes.
- **M1**: Angstrom and high-level coherence, wrapped sunpy maps, the #2595 pair matrix, SJI click to raster spectrum, and DN/s.
- **M3**: per-scan stack WCS, NEXP_PRP > 1, pointing offsets and an IRIS–SST Level-3 pair.

Every WP1 PR carries a changelog fragment and the matching WP9 guide change.

**Port from prototypes**

- **M0 link port.** Port these into M0 (`wp1-m0-link-hpc`, `wp1-m0-axis-names`, `wp1-m0-inverse-workaround`):
  - `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp1/glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py`: `link_hpc` and the `world_axis_names` precedence hunk.
  - `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp1/glue_solar/sources/iris.py`: `add_link(link_hpc(...))` after `app.add_datasets` in `browse_iris`, the `link_iris` menubar action, and `__all__`.
  - `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp1/glue_solar/glue_patches.py`, and its import in `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp1/glue_solar/__init__.py`.

  Fix these first:
  - Keep the `"time"` entry deleted from `_AXIS_NAMES`. With the entry kept, an SJI gets two components labelled `Time`, and `data.id['Time']` silently returns None.
  - WP0 registers `glue_patches` against glue #2598 (wp1-links-8, archive-trace-7).
  - followup-4-4: once `link_hpc` is installed, a stock raster ROI costs about 10 s for each full-resolution SJI frame. Before `browse_iris` installs `link_hpc` by default, `wp10-m0-acceptance` must record that per-frame cost. The guide documents the freeze in browser-opened viewers until `wp10-m1-roi-world-polygon` (default, confirm). The alternative is to extend `wp10-m0-roi-guard` to those viewers.
- **M1 wrapper hunk.** Port the `_GlueWCS` unit and high-level hunk of `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp1/glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py` into M1 `wp1-m1-wrapper-coherence`. The hunk covers `_AXIS_UNITS`, `_units`, the converting value methods, `world_axis_object_components` with `_converting_getter`, and `world_axis_object_classes` with `_converting_constructor`. final.markdown:
### WP2: Line moments and diagnostics

WP2 turns IRIS spectra into derived maps. Each product is a D4 `layer_action` (`glue_qt.config.layer_action`). The action rewraps the selected Data as an irispy cube and leaves the numerics to irispy, apart from the continuum mean and the saturation/+Inf guard. It adds no required dependency, and it adds one linked Data without opening a viewer. The primary paths are `glue_solar/sources/moments.py` (new, imported from `glue_solar.setup()`), `glue_solar/tests/test_moments.py`, a new page under `docs/user_guide/` and `changelog/`. WP2 has no M0 or M1 work. M2 is done when 'IRIS: line moments…' on a per-scan raster window adds intensity, centroid, sigma, velocity and continuum maps. These use the D11 rest wavelength, Angstrom (D3) and km/s, and they carry a uint8 mask, two pixel links, WP3 session support and a Worker for large windows. M3 adds 4D stacks, wings from a Profile range, dust removal and radiometric calibration, uncertainties with error maps and binning, Mg II features, density/temperature maps and UV bursts. Each of these waits for irispy wherever irispy lacks the numerics.

**Port from prototypes**

- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/chk_wp2/wp2_moments_module.py` → `glue_solar/sources/moments.py`: port `line_moments`, `_in_angstrom`, `_number`, `MomentsDialog` and `moments_action`, keeping the DN·Å integrated threshold and the `Time` copy. Fix these first:
  - Blank wings mean the whole window (:72; wp2-wp6-science-2).
  - The rest is prefilled from TWAVE (:66-69), and :35 passes the SGMeta. `calculate_moments` falls back to `cube.meta.rest_wavelength` (TWAVE) whenever rest is None (utils/moments.py:100-101@0.9.0), so a blank rest still gives TWAVE velocities. The port must always pass the centre explicitly (wp2-wp6-science-1, wp3-wp5-1).
  - Maps built through `_cube_data` (:43) carry irispy's 2-axis -TAB WCS, which WP3 cannot save (wp2-wp6-science-10, wp3-wp5-3).
  - The rest actually used is not written to meta (wp2-wp6-science-16).
  - Inf samples are zeroed before the saturation test (wp2-wp6-science-8).
  - The width component is named `width` (wp2-wp6-science-13).
  - The run is synchronous (:87; followup-2-7), and it reads `data.coords._wcs` without the WP10 lock (:35; followup-2-1).
  - Negative-step rasters give wrong results until `wp10-m0-negative-step` lands (followup-4-2).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/chk_wp2/test_wp2_moments.py` → `glue_solar/tests/test_moments.py`: port all five tests. Fix these first:
  - The fixture names (:25, :106) fail on irispy 0.9.0. Use `find_irispy_test_file` from `glue_solar/conftest.py` (wp2-wp6-science-17).
  - Take the wavelength step from the WCS instead of the hard-coded 0.02546 (:97).
  - Move the TWAVE expectation (:37) and `IN_WINDOW_REST` (:13) to the new rest/wings policy.

  Also port two checks from the archive-verdict `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp2_moments_proto.py`. The first is that a window without a policy rest gives no TWAVE velocity maps (:139-140). The second is that `_can_trigger` enables the action on datasets but not on subsets (:160-166). With these fixes, the three prototype test files (WP2, WP6, line positions) gave 13 passed on iris-plan, against 3 failed, 10 passed and 3 errors before.

**M2**

- [ ] **M2** `wp2-m2-moment-maps`: Port the 'IRIS: line moments…' `layer_action` (data only, single selection) into `glue_solar/sources/moments.py`. A rewrap helper builds an irispy `SpectrogramCube` from a per-scan raster Data: the chosen component, its mask, its unit and a `copy.deepcopy` of the raw WCS, taken while holding the `wp10-m0-wcs-lock` lock. The helper calls `irispy.utils.moments.calculate_moments` with an explicit centre, and it refuses SJIs and 4D stacks with a message. The action adds one Data:
  - Components: `intensity`, a uint8 `mask` (D12), `centroid` and `sigma` in Å, `velocity` and `sigma_velocity` in km/s, and the source `Time` at wavelength index 0.

**Notes and limits**

- Profile Collapse offers Mean, Median, Minimum, Maximum, Sum, Moment 1 and Moment 2 (glue-qt profile_tools.py:31-37@0.4.2), but it is not WP2. It only sets an AggregateSlice on Image viewers of the same data and creates no dataset. Its Moment 1 and 2 are computed from the index within the selected sub-range, and one NaN sample makes the moment NaN (core aggregate.py:8-26). That makes it a display-only quicklook. Maps that are calibrated, saved and linked need WP2's `layer_action` (D4).
- Velocities are relative to the uncorrected Level-2 wavelength scale, because irispy 0.9.0 has no orbital or thermal drift correction (see the WP5 caveat). Mg II h/k and C II centroids and widths are proxies, not line-of-sight velocities.
- The +Inf guard answers a code path, not a demonstrated real-data defect. Local int16 Level-2 files (BSCALE 0.25, BZERO 7992) cannot store Inf, and all of them show NSATPIX 0.
- Why the Worker: the moments block the GUI thread for 0.6 s on the 2018 windows and 2.2 s on sit-and-stare Si IV. These are local acceptance numbers, not CI thresholds.
- Thread safety: the module-level `wp10-m0-wcs-lock` covers only `_GlueWCS` calls, not reads of the raw astropy WCS. So the rewrap takes its deep copy while holding the lock, and the Worker computes on that copy. The map coords wrap the same copy, which leaves the map sharing no astropy WCS with its source.
- WP0 tracks the upstream irispy work: uncertainty propagation in `calculate_moments`, Mg II k/h feature extraction, UV burst detection, and the negative-step flip of the mask and uncertainty.

### WP3: Sessions

File > Save Session and Open Session must work on released glue-core 1.27.0 / glue-qt 0.4.2, both for a coordinated IRIS quicklook and for every glue-solar dataset: SJI, raster windows, stacks, sunpy Maps and derived maps. The work uses glue's own `__gluestate__` hooks and `@saver`/`@loader` registry, not a second session system. It touches `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py`, `glue_solar/sources/maps.py`, `glue_solar/sources/loaders/maps.py`, `glue_solar/__init__.py`, `glue_solar/tests/test_sessions.py` (new), `docs/user_guide/loading-iris-level-2-raster-and-sji-data.rst` and `docs/user_guide/loading-aia-and-hmi.rst`. M0 has no WP3 work. Until WP3 lands, the docs say that sessions containing any glue-solar dataset, including File→Open sunpy Maps, fail to save on released core; WP9 owns that text. M1 is done when a real-data quicklook saves and reopens twice, its coordination still works, the session stays within the size budget and the unsupported-session warning has been replaced. M3 adds reopening the last session.

  - The first time the WP4 quicklook entry runs in an application, connect that app's `QApplication.aboutToQuit`. Never connect it in `setup()`, which runs in every glue-qt process, `glue -g` and tests included.
  - The handler first sums the bytes of the components that glue would embed: those with no `_load_log` that are not a `DerivedComponent`, a `BroadcastComponent` or a coordinate component. If the sum exceeds 1 MB, it returns.
  - Otherwise it calls `GlueSerializer(app, absolute_paths=True).dumps()` directly, catching every exception silently. It never calls `app.save_session`, whose `@catch_error` opens a modal dialog.
  - Only if the result is ≤ 1 MB and took ≤ 2 s does it write a temp file and `os.replace` it to `iris_last_session.glu` under `glue.config.CFG_DIR`, which it reads at call time.

  - a serialization error writes nothing and opens no dialog.

**Notes and limits**

- Sessions record `glue_solar` class and function paths, so loading them needs glue-solar and its Qt imports.
  - While the solar Quantity pair is active, any session with Quantity metadata that was saved in a glue-solar process also needs glue-solar, and Quantity subclasses come back as plain `Quantity` (wp3-wp5-5).
  - WP3 is a scoped glue-solar representation, not a generic core fix for low-level WCS wrappers or `clone(link)`. It adds no generic `-TAB` framework and no dependencies beyond `asdf` and `gwcs`.
- Derived-map contract (wp3-wp5-3): WP2 moment maps, WP6 fit maps and every other derived spatial map use `_GlueWCS(SlicedLowLevelWCS(raw_wcs, slices))`. Unwrap the source once, slice its raw WCS and rewrap once.
  - A bare outer sliced wrapper and irispy's `dropaxis` 2-D `-TAB` template are not covered, and either one makes the whole save fail.
  - Any new coords type on glue-solar data (WP12 `wp12-time-regrid`, WP1 `wp1-stack-per-scan-wcs`, `wp1-m3-pointing-offset`) either uses a record kind that `wp3-wcs-saver` already has, for example a plain FITS WCS wrapped in `_GlueWCS`, or adds one. Either way it adds a round-trip case to `test_sessions.py`.
- Ordering: `wp3-style-cmap` on its own makes File→Open sunpy-Map sessions work, because their coords are a raw astropy WCS that glue saves natively. `wp1-m1-sunpy-maps` (D3) wraps those coords in `_GlueWCS`, so it merges after `wp3-wcs-saver` or together with it, and map sessions never regress.
- LoadLog cannot replace the WCS saver, because glue saves `data.coords` for every dataset (`_save_data`@1.27.0; wp3-wp5-18).
  - If irispy's `gwcs_raster_clean` lands with custom transforms that have no ASDF converters, combined-raster sessions fail. That lasts until irispy ships converters (WP0, upstream-state-2) or the record re-derives the WCS from the re-read file.
  - D14 keeps M0 on irispy 0.9.0 and gates `gwcs_raster_clean`. The saver is tested on 0.9.0 and retested on each irispy release.
- On 1.27.0, every IRIS spectrum panel fails to restore, because `x_att` and `x_display_unit` share restore priority. WP0 owns the gated patch and the core PR (`wp0-core-profile-restore-priority`, wp3-wp5-2), and `wp3-app-session-acceptance` is their end-to-end check.
- Known gaps:
  - 'Include data' sessions embed every array, including the broadcast `Time` and `Exposure time`, and are not budgeted.
  - The colormap combo shows the first colormap with an identical lookup table, so `sdoaia171` is labelled GOES-R SUVI 171. This is cosmetic.
  - Restored image layers come from `get_layer_artist`, not `layer_artist_maker`, so WP11's added percentile choices return only if WP11 re-applies them through a registered viewer tool.
  - Restored datasets have no SGMeta, so WP2's M3 calibration actions refuse them.

issues.where: wp4-time-sync (SJI master bullet, done-when 1) and wp4-point-fixed-index done-when
issues.problem: With an SJI master the draft 'retargets the point's acquisition index (raster step, exposure, or stack (scan, step))', so playing the SJI sweeps the held point across the step (spatial x) axis of a scanning raster or stack. That contradicts D7 (fixed detector pixel) and F111/F112, where the raster timing step represents a raster frame and the cursor never moves. It also contradicts the draft's own point-fixed-index check 'the point stays fixed while the scan or exposure is stepped'. The spatial rasters feasibility note (feas coordination/master) says 'A spatial 3D raster has no time axis, so it only shows its offset'.
issues.fix: Rewrite the SJI-master rule. An SJI master moves only true time axes: a sit-and-stare point's exposure, and a stack's scan, chosen as the scan whose Time at the point's step (the timing step) is nearest. It never moves a step or slit. A single scanning raster only shows its signed offset or NO MATCH for the timing step; the M1 map line shows the step exposed at the master time. Change done-when (1) to: 'with the SJI as master, frames 0-15 select scan 0 and frames 16-31 select scan 1, the point's step and slit are unchanged, and the readout shows Δt against Time[scan, point step]'. Keep the measured nearest (scan, step) values only as the oracle for the wp4-raster-overlays map line. In point-fixed-index, reword the check to 'the point's step and slit stay fixed while the scan, exposure or SJI master is stepped'.

issues.where: wp4-point-fixed-index (whole checkbox; 'It never writes a wavelength slice')
issues.problem: Only map clicks are defined. If the user clicks with Pixel on the spectrogram, whisker or λ–t panel, glue writes PixelSubsetState(λ=k, slit=y, step=slice(None)) into the same group (pixel_selection_mode.py:56-65). That replaces the point, so the 'spectrum' becomes a single-wavelength mean over steps and the coordinator has no step to propagate. The disposition wp4-quicklook-13 mapping row, 'a point on the spectrogram sets the map wavelength and the point's slit', is dropped, and 'never writes a wavelength slice' contradicts it with no recorded reason.
issues.fix: Add a rule and a check. The coordinator canonicalises a Pixel state created on a non-map panel of a coordinated dataset. It rebuilds the point as (that panel's fixed step, exposure or scan; the clicked slit) and, for a spectrogram click, writes the clicked λ into the map's wavelength slice, per wp4-quicklook-13. Restrict 'never writes a wavelength slice' to time sync and map clicks. Done when a spectrogram click at (λj, y) on 4000005156 scan 0 moves the map to λj, puts the point at (s, y) and leaves the spectrum a full λ profile equal to cube[s, y, :].

final.markdown:
### WP5: Spectral units, rest wavelength, line list, blink and Doppler

WP5 gives IRIS spectra a D11 rest wavelength, km/s views, line labels, CRISPEX-style blink and the Doppler wing-difference image. Everything uses glue registries (D2) on the released glue-core 1.27.0 / glue-qt 0.4.2. The code goes in these files:
- `glue_solar/spectral.py` is new and replaces the old plan's `glue_solar/viewers.py`. It holds the rest helper, the unit converter, the line-list artist, the layer_actions and the derived-product helper.
- `glue_solar/tools.py` holds the blink and km/s-axis tools.
- `glue_solar/data/iris_lines.csv` is the packaged line list.
- `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py` writes the plain meta keys.
- `setup()` in `glue_solar/__init__.py` does the registration, and tests go in `glue_solar/tests/`.

WP5 has no M0 work. M1 is done when the rest policy, the km/s top axis and converter, the line list, same-cube and cross-window blink, and the Doppler image all pass their real-data checks on the released baseline. Each lands with its user-guide section and changelog fragment. M3 adds rest wavelengths taken from measurements, reference blink and mean-spectrum subtraction.

**Port from prototypes**

- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/iris_lines.csv` -> `glue_solar/data/iris_lines.csv`, shipped as tracked package data (include-package-data plus setuptools_scm). Fix first: the rows and columns listed in `wp5-m1-line-list` (wp3-wp5-9, followup-3-14).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_units.py` -> the `u.doppler_optical` `to_unit` and `install()`, which replaces `unit_converter.members['default']`. Call it from `setup()`, not at import (:54). Fix first:
  - Keep the stock unit lists and only append km/s (usefulness-6, wp3-wp5-6).
  - Wrap the stock `equivalent_units` in `list()`, because it returns a `map` (glue/core/units.py:52-53@1.27.0).
  - Reduce `rest_wavelength` to reading one plain meta key, with no SGMeta or TWAVE fallback (wp3-wp5-1, wp2-wp6-science-1, archive-trace-4, archive-trace-3, wp3-wp5-4, wp2-wp6-science-16, archive-trace-13).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_override.py` -> only the layer_action body (:13-28). Fix first: drop the import side effects and the demo (:2-5, :31-48), replace the key pop at :26 with the Reset rule of `wp5-m1-rest-wavelength-policy`, and add the picker for lines inside the window (wp3-wp5-1, wp3-wp5-12).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_linelist_mod.py` -> `LineListState`, `LineListArtist` and the `line_list_artist` maker. Fix first:
  - Use `np.interp` instead of `brentq` (:3, :99), which also drops scipy (wp3-wp5-17).
  - Delete the exact-class style dict (:116-118, wp3-wp5-15).
  - Keep the list a plain table (core-qt-capabilities-4, upstream-state-6).
  - The menubar entry has no prototype and is new code (wp3-wp5-12).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_blink.py` -> the CheckableTool + QTimer skeleton with its restore on deactivate and close. Register it in `setup()` instead of the module-level edit (:67-68). Fix first: no permanent toolbar spinbox (:31-38, wp3-wp5-16), and alternate (dataset, slices) pairs instead of layers (usefulness-14, followup-3-6).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_label.py` -> not ported to glue-solar. It becomes the optional glue-core PR `wp0-core-profile-unit-label` (archive-trace-8).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260905/test_line_positions.py` -> `glue_solar/tests/test_linelist.py`, both tests. Add:
  - an IRIS-raster multi-axis session case, xfailed until `wp0-core-profile-restore-priority` (wp3-wp5-2);
  - the layer-colour and float-rest checks from `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/archive/2026-09-23-prototype-refresh/wp5_ll_session.py`. Its km/s check waits for the km/s gate in `wp5-m1-velocity-axis`.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260905/test_refresh.py` -> only `test_blink_close_restores_original_visibility`, rewritten against the production tool in `glue_solar/tests/test_blink.py`. The file's other tests belong to WP4.

**M1**

- [ ] **M1** `wp5-m1-line-list`: Package `glue_solar/data/iris_lines.csv` with the columns `wavelength` (vacuum Å), `name`, `source` (NIST ASD, CHIANTI or a paper), `default_for` (a TDESC) and `calibration`.
  - Keep the 11 lines and add Fe XII 1349.40, Mg II 2791.60/2798.75/2798.82, O IV 1404.78, S IV 1404.81/1406.02, Ni I 2799.474 and S I 1401.515. Use Fe XXI 1354.106 (Young, Tian and Jaeggli 2015), and flag Ni I, S I and O I 1355.598 as calibration lines.
  - `default_for` maps each TDESC to its default line: Fe XII 1349 → 1349.40, Cl I 1352 → 1351.657, O I 1356 → 1355.598, Si IV 1394 → 1393.755, Si IV 1403 → 1402.770, and Mg II k 2796 → both k 2796.352 and h 2803.53. C II 1336 has no default.

**Notes and limits**

- Velocities are relative to the uncorrected Level-2 wavelength scale (±5–10 km/s), and irispy 0.9.0 has no drift correction. Mg II and C II velocities are optically thick proxies, which WP2 labels as such. Image-axis velocity and generic annotation frameworks are out of scope, and sliders always show wavelength.
- km/s as a Profile x display unit waits for a glue-qt release containing #70. On 0.4.2, both Navigate and Collapse compare the display-unit x with native values (glue_qt/viewers/profile/profile_tools.py:163-175, 302-333@0.4.2). With any non-native unit, nm included, they land on the wrong slice (slice 28 instead of 20). Until then, km/s appears on the top axis, in the WP11 readout and in product meta, and the preset keeps Profiles in native Å (after WP1).
- Doppler image, three deviations and limits:
  - It keeps an Å axis instead of the km/s axis that wp3-wp5-11 asks for. This keeps the one WP3 derived-map contract (wp3-wp5-3) instead of editing irispy's -TAB raster WCS. The velocity comes from the WP11 readout.
  - It does not follow the source map's wavelength, which is a known part of the F148 gap. The WP4 Doppler-mirror marker shows the pairing.
  - The product is float32, has at most half the source's wavelength planes, and embeds its array in sessions.
- Blink scope:
  - Temporal blink (N↔N+k), bounce/CYCLE, frame sub-ranges and playback slower than 2 fps belong to `wp4-time-controls`, and the raster timing offset belongs to WP4's M0 mapping table.
  - The blink settings cannot go in a menu, because glue-qt 0.4.2 never attaches `menu_actions()` to a CheckableTool (toolbar.py:106-192@0.4.2).
- Why the converter is replaced in place: `add()` refuses an existing label, and a new converter name would be saved in settings.cfg and break glue's startup without glue-solar. No style-editor patch is needed, because the stock class-valued `ProfileViewer._layer_style_widget_cls` already gives both line layers and later stock layers a ProfileLayerStyleEditor (probe on iris-plan, 2026-09-27).
- Upstream: glue #2603 / glue-qt #73 line layers (`wp0-track-line-layers`) would add labels on spectrogram and whisker images and replace `LineListArtist` once released. Image-axis labels are tested only then. Pyoung's 91-line CHIANTI table is not adopted, because its licence is unchecked.

final.markdown:
### WP6: Gaussian fit maps

WP6 fits a Gaussian to every spectrum of an IRIS raster window. It is a D4 dataset `layer_action` that adds one linked parameter-map dataset and opens no viewer. It also registers single-spectrum Gaussian fitters for the stock Profile Fit tab. Primary paths: `glue_solar/sources/fitting.py` (new), `glue_solar/__init__.py` (`setup()` registration), `glue_solar/tests/test_fitting.py`, `glue_solar/tests/test_sessions.py`, `docs/user_guide/`. WP6 has no M0 or M1 work. M2 is done when single Gaussian + constant maps are fitted on the valid samples inside a fit window, quality- and saturation-filtered, published with a velocity from the WP5 rest and computed in a Worker without touching the shared WCS; when fit products stay small in sessions; and when the Fit-tab fitters work on point and ROI spectra. M3 is done when red-blue asymmetry drives per-pixel double-Gaussian (proxy) fits, and line-list-seeded weighted template fits publish error maps.

**Port from prototypes**

- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_fitting.py` → `glue_solar/sources/fitting.py`. Port `wavelength_angstrom`, the single-Gaussian path of `fit_gaussians`, `gaussian_fit_data` (with its `_GlueWCS(SlicedLowLevelWCS(raw_wcs, slices))` coords), `add_fit_products` without the default residual, `_ask`, `start_fit` (with `_WORKERS` and the progress-dialog reference at :155) and `fit_gaussians_action`. Fix these first:
  - Replace the clip and `nan_to_num` at :61: build `mask = ~isfinite(window)`, set `window[mask] = 0` (and `weights[mask] = 0` when weights are used), then pass `mask=`. Do not clip negative values and do not touch unmasked samples (wp2-wp6-science-3).
  - Seed from the mean of the valid samples, not the plain mean at :63 (wp2-wp6-science-8).
  - Replace `Const1D + Gaussian1D` with the shared unbounded named-parameter model (see `wp6-m2-profile-fitter`).
  - Add the quality and saturation filter. Publish |sigma| where amplitude > 0; do not reject those fits (wp2-wp6-science-4).
  - Make the float64 residual at :89/:123 opt-in and float32 (followup-2-4, wp2-wp6-science-12).
  - Keep the Worker away from the WCS. It currently runs :32 and :101-113; the `SlicedLowLevelWCS` at :104 calls `axis_correlation_matrix` in its constructor, and :103 reads `coords._wcs` directly (followup-2-1).
  - Add the fit window and the velocity products (wp2-wp6-science-7).
  - Move the 'Mg II k2v/k2r' label at :132 to M3 as a proxy (wp2-wp6-science-6).
  - Rename `width` to `sigma`, and stop storing the seed at :105 as `rest_wavelength_angstrom` (wp2-wp6-science-13, wp2-wp6-science-16, archive-trace-13).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_test_fitting.py` → `glue_solar/tests/test_fitting.py`: all 7 test functions (8 collected items). Fix these first:
  - Replace the exact fixture names at :114/:139 with `find_irispy_test_file`.
  - Update the 0.8.1 window asserts at :117-120; they fail on irispy 0.9.0 full windows (wp2-wp6-science-17). Pass an explicit window of at least ±2 Å: the 0.9.0 fixtures step 0.254 Å, so the default ±0.5 Å holds about 4 samples for 4 parameters and every spectrum would be NaN'd.
  - Change the residual-on-source asserts at :103-105 and :153 for the opt-in residual.
  - Update the expectations for masked samples.

  Port `recovers_synthetic_parameters[2]` and `test_double_gaussian_seeds_at_the_given_centre` only with the M3 double Gaussian.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_test_fitting_final.py` → merge only its two `worker.progress.isVisible()` asserts (:156, :160) into the `test_fitting.py` port, then archive the file.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260905/test_plan_integration.py` → `glue_solar/tests/test_sessions.py`, after `wp3-wcs-saver` lands. Port only `test_wp3_roundtrips_wp6_fitted_map`. Fix these first:
  - Drop `import wp3_impl`, `importlib.import_module(module_name)` and the `module_name` parametrize, which also removes `wp6_fitting_brief` (usefulness-7). Import `glue_solar.sources.fitting` and rely on the production `_GlueWCS.__gluestate__` (D13).
  - The test uses a plain FITS WCS (:52-58), so add a WP2 -TAB moments-map variant beside it (wp3-wp5-3). WP6 owns both variants; the moments variant waits for `wp2-m2-moment-maps`.
  - Drop the stubbed quicklook test (wp4-quicklook-15) and the WP8 `.ui` test (WP8's own port covers it).
- Keep as test evidence:
  - `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_chk_real_fixed.{py,log}`: log lines 21-23 are the only recorded 4-D stack fit, with maps (13, 8, 109); the `.py` generated them (recipe at :63-68). Keep both until the 4-D test lands.
  - `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_full_raster.{py,log}`: a full 2018 window of 320×548 spectra took 25.3 s with processes and 152.6 s single-threaded. It is the baseline for the WP6 budget until that budget has a recorded check.

**M2**

- [ ] **M2** `wp6-m2-fit-maps`: Port the fit as the D4 `layer_action` 'IRIS: Gaussian fit maps…' (`glue_qt.config.layer_action`) in `glue_solar/sources/fitting.py`, imported from `setup()`. Fit the shared unbounded Gaussian + constant model (`wp6-m2-profile-fitter`) with `LMLSQFitter` through astropy `parallel_fit_dask`. The flux component is chosen in the dialog; the default is WP1's '<flux> DN/s' when present, else the first main component, as in `wp2-m2-input-quality`. Fit only inside a window taken from the WP2 rest/wings fields. The default window is the WP5 rest ± 0.5 Å and can be edited. Without a rest, the user enters the window, velocity outputs are off and the dialog says why.
  - Masking: after `wp10-fill-nan`, missing samples are NaN in the already-flipped data, so `mask = ~isfinite(window)` and no irispy mask term is needed (D10, followup-4-2). Set `window[mask] = 0`, then pass `mask=`. parallel_fit_dask applies the mask only as zero weights (`_fitting_parallel.py:505-510`@astropy 8.0.1), and a NaN left under a zero weight makes the whole fit NaN (checked on iris-plan). Do not clip and do not apply `nan_to_num` to unmasked samples. NaN every parameter of a spectrum whose valid samples are ≤ the number of free parameters.
  - Seeding: seed from the mean of the valid samples. An optional in-window seed centre overrides it. Never seed from TWAVE, and add no mean-spectrum prefit.

issues.where: wp6-m2-fit-maps (Masking bullet) and Port from prototypes, wp6_fitting.py fix 1
issues.problem: The draft says to pass `mask=` and forbids `nan_to_num`, but it never says to make the masked samples finite. parallel_fit_dask applies the mask only as zero weights (`_fitting_parallel.py:505-510`) and NaN-skips only all-NaN spectra (:203). LM's residual is then 0*NaN = NaN, so every partly missing spectrum fails and comes back NaN. Once wp10-fill-nan NaN-fills -200/-199, that is every spectrum with a gap. I checked this on iris-plan (astropy 8.0.1): a spectrum with 3 NaN samples and another with one Inf gave NaN with mask= alone, and the right fit once the masked samples were zeroed. This contradicts the finding's own recommendation ('zero only those samples').
issues.fix: Reword to: 'Build mask = loader mask | ~isfinite(data), set data[mask] = 0 (and weights[mask] = 0 when weights are used), then pass mask=. Do not clip negative values and do not apply nan_to_num to unmasked samples.' Put the same wording in port fix 1. Add to the done_when that partly masked spectra of the synthetic cube get finite fits.

issues.problem: The checkbox says each fitter is 'an AstropyFitter1D subclass over the same Const1D + Gaussian1D model'. AstropyFitter1D builds the model as `self.model_cls(**params)` and reads `model_cls.param_names` (glue/core/fitters.py:218-238@1.27.0). `models.Const1D + models.Gaussian1D` cannot be a class: adding the two classes raises TypeError on astropy 8.0.1 (checked). The bundle's `custom_model` detail was dropped. Also, if the fitter reuses LMLSQFitter, fitting the bounded Gaussian1D raises AstropyDeprecationWarning (checked), which fails every Fit-tab test under `filterwarnings = error`.
issues.fix: State that the shared model is a named-parameter `custom_model` or `Fittable1DModel` (background, amplitude, mean, stddev; for two Gaussians, amplitude_1/mean_1/stddev_1/amplitude_2/…) in `glue_solar/sources/fitting.py`, used both as `model_cls` and in the per-pixel fit. Set `fitting_cls` to LevMarLSQFitter or TRFLSQFitter, not LMLSQFitter.

issues.problem: `calculate_red_blue_asymmetry(rest_wavelength=None)` falls back silently to SGMeta TWAVE (red_blue.py:125,146-149@0.9.0), which D11 forbids. 'Supports continuum windows' can be read as running on spectral windows that have no rest; D11 says those get no km/s. The item also puts the irispy call in the Worker, but the function needs an irispy SpectrogramCube with a WCS, so the Worker would use the shared -TAB WCS, which is the followup-2-1 crash class.
issues.fix: Always pass `rest_wavelength` explicitly from the WP5 policy, and refuse the action with a message when the policy gives no rest. Say that 'continuum windows' means irispy's `continuum_windows` fit ranges. Build the cube with WP2's rewrap helper, which takes a `copy.deepcopy` of the raw WCS, so the Worker never touches the shared WCS. Add `wp2-m2-moment-maps` (rewrap helper) to Depends.

issues.problem: Gaussian1D has a default stddev bound, and astropy 8.0.1 deprecates LMLSQFitter on bounded models: a direct call raises AstropyDeprecationWarning (checked with -W error). parallel_fit_dask records the warning inside its catch_warnings, so the prototype never showed it. That hides a deprecated path which a future astropy may remove. Any direct LMLSQFitter reference fit in tests will error under pytest.ini.
issues.fix: Either remove the bound (`Gaussian1D(..., bounds={'stddev': (None, None)})`, which fits the |sigma| policy) or use TRFLSQFitter by default. Record the deprecation in Notes, and state that reference fits in tests use the same unbounded model or a non-deprecated fitter.

issues.where: wp6-m2-products / wp6-m2-worker (main-thread WCS build) and cross_wp_notes WP10
issues.problem: Moving the `SlicedLowLevelWCS(raw_wcs, …)` build to the main thread does not make it safe. Its constructor calls `raw_wcs.axis_correlation_matrix` directly on the unwrapped astropy WCS, outside the `_GlueWCS` lock. The glue-qt Profile ComputeWorker can be inside the same WCS at that moment. The feasibility risk for followup-2-1 names 'the WP6 raw_wcs' as unprotected. The WP10 cross-note ('WP6 relies on the lock only for GUI-thread and Profile-worker access') misses this.
issues.fix: Require the map WCS (and any `coords._wcs` read) to be built while holding the WP10 module-level `_GlueWCS` RLock, through a small helper exported next to `_GlueWCS`. Add a test that builds the maps while a thread loops on the source's `pixel_to_world_values`. Update the WP10 cross-note to ask for that helper.

issues.problem: The note says Inf flags saturation and that the WP6 mask catches it. The feasibility verifier (F164 note, which wins) says Level-2 saturation is the top int16 code, which scales to about 16182 DN, and that the loader leaves it alone. Saturated real samples are therefore fitted as data. WP2 (`wp2-m2-input-quality`) NaNs pixels whose in-wing peak exceeds a DN saturation limit or that contain +Inf. WP6 has no equivalent, so the two products disagree.
issues.fix: Correct the note: Level-2 int16 saturation appears as about 16182 DN, not Inf. Add to the quality filter: reuse WP2's saturation check (DN limit plus +Inf inside the fit window), NaN those spectra, count them in the rejected fraction, and warn on NSATPIX/TSATPXn > 0.

issues.where: wp6-m2-fit-maps (flux component default) and Notes (DN/s bullet)
issues.problem: WP6 defaults to 'the first main component' (DN). `wp2-m2-input-quality` makes '<flux> DN/s' the default when it exists, and wp2-wp6-science-9 recommends DN/s by default for amplitude maps. The note says WP6 follows WP2's exposure-normalisation checkbox, but the default contradicts it.
issues.fix: Default to WP1's '<flux> DN/s' component when present, as `wp2-m2-input-quality` does, and apply the quality and saturation thresholds in the chosen unit. Add `wp1-dn-per-s` to Depends as a soft dependency, and cite `wp2-m2-input-quality` by key in Notes.

issues.problem: Several keys do not match the sibling drafts. The WP2 draft renamed `wp2-m3-calibrated-window-data` to `wp2-m3-window-data`, and the rest/wings fields are in `wp2-m2-line-definition`, not `wp2-m2-moment-maps`. The WP3 session budget is `wp3-session-budget`, not `wp3-app-session-acceptance`. 'The WP3 port' is `wp3-wcs-saver`. The wavelength-calibration caveat that wp6-m2-rest-key copies is `wp5-wavecal-caveat`.
issues.fix: wp6-m2-fit-maps: Depends `wp2-m2-line-definition`. wp6-m2-products: `wp3-session-budget`. wp6-m2-tests: `wp3-wcs-saver`. wp6-m3-template-fits and old_trace: `wp2-m3-window-data`. wp6-m2-rest-key: add `wp5-wavecal-caveat`. Fix the matching cross_wp_notes (WP2 note: 'depends on wp2-m2-line-definition').

issues.where: Port from prototypes, keep-as-test-evidence bullet; cross_wp_notes housekeeping
issues.problem: Only `wp6_chk_real_fixed.log` is kept. The protos verifier note says `wp6_chk_real_fixed.py` generated that 4-D evidence (recipe at :63-68) and must be kept with it, and the general prototype table in drafts/rest.md already lists `wp6_chk_real_fixed.{py,log}`.
issues.fix: Keep `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_chk_real_fixed.{py,log}` together until the 4-D test lands, and update the housekeeping cross-note the same way.

issues.where: Port from prototypes, test_plan_integration.py bullet; cross_wp_notes WP3
issues.problem: Ownership of the WP2 -TAB moments round-trip variant conflicts. The WP6 draft says WP2 owns it. The protos verdict (port_what: 'plus a WP2 moments-map variant', port_to WP6) and the WP3 draft (WP3.md Port list: 'WP6 owns this port at M2 and adds a WP2 -TAB moments variant') give it to WP6.
issues.fix: Pick one owner. Either WP6 ports it beside its own round trip, depending on `wp2-m2-moment-maps`, as the verdict says. Or keep WP2 as owner, point to `wp2-m2-moment-maps`'s WP3 round-trip done_when, and add a cross_wp_note telling WP3 to change its Port-list line.

issues.problem: The test imports `wp3_impl` to install the prototype savers, and loads the fit module through `importlib.import_module(module_name)`. Porting it as written breaks D13, which says production never imports prototype modules. The draft does not say to replace these imports.
issues.fix: Add to the port fixes: drop `import wp3_impl` and the `module_name` parametrize, and import `glue_solar.sources.fitting` and rely on the production `_GlueWCS.__gluestate__` from `wp3-wcs-saver`.

issues.problem: The mask ORs in the 'loader mask'. On negative-step rasters irispy builds its mask before the flip (D10, followup-4-2), so until that WP10 fix lands, valid samples are masked and the wrong ones kept. WP2's moments item lists this dependency; WP6 does not.
issues.fix: Add 'the WP10 negative-step mask fix (followup-4-2, D10)' to Depends. Alternatively, state that after wp10-fill-nan the mask is `~isfinite(data)` alone, and drop the loader-mask term.

issues.where: Notes and limits (first bullet), F157 coverage
issues.problem: Ierr/Verr (fit-parameter error maps), which are among IDL's six products in F157's gap, are 'out of M2', but no later checkbox picks them up. wp6-m3-template-fits adds weights but no error maps, so the gap is left open without saying so.
issues.fix: Either add to wp6-m3-template-fits: 'when weighted, publish 1σ parameter errors (amplitude_error, centroid_error, velocity_error) from per-pixel fit_info param_cov'. Or state in Notes that Ierr/Verr are a non-goal, with the reason.

issues.problem: 'per-pixel fit_info from parallel_fit_dask(fit_info=...)' leaves the argument open. `fit_info=True` stores the whole OptimizeResult per pixel (jac, fun, grad and so on) and makes the Dask result array dtype=object (`_fitting_parallel.py:730`). On 175k spectra run through processes, that is a large, avoidable cost. The sigma == 0 case is also not handled: |0| is published even though the done_when forbids sigma ≤ 0.
issues.fix: Specify `fit_info=('status',)` on a fitter instance, read `fitter.fit_info.get_property_as_array('status')`, and treat status ≤ 0 as not converged. NaN fits with sigma == 0.

issues.problem: 'Recovers amplitude, centroid and sigma' has no tolerance. 'The change is recorded' is a measurement, not a pass/fail condition. Requiring 'fewer valid samples than free parameters' allows fits with zero degrees of freedom. On the 0.9.0 fixtures (0.254 Å step), the default ±0.5 Å window holds about 4 samples for 4 parameters, so fixture tests would be exactly determined or fail.
issues.fix: Give tolerances (for example, within 3σ of the noise-propagated error, or rtol 5% for amplitude and sigma and 0.005 Å for the centroid). Make the Si IV comparison assert that both runs complete and that the Si IV centroid shift is written to the test output. NaN spectra with valid samples ≤ free parameters. Have fixture tests pass an explicit wider window.

issues.problem: 'Match a direct astropy fit … in both m and Å display' does not say what the reference fit is. A reference fit in metres can be as ill-conditioned as the Fit tab and still match it. It is also unclear whether the 1e-6 match applies to the two-Gaussian fitter too. That fitter is not labelled as a Mg II proxy (wp2-wp6-science-6).
issues.fix: Define the reference as a direct fit in Å on the same finite samples and seeds, with the m-display result converted to Å. Say which fitter(s) the tolerance covers, and call it proposed. Label the two-Gaussian fitter as a proxy for Mg II/C II in its label or the guide.

issues.problem: 'the work-5 fixture' is a session scratch name that means nothing in the public plan. `wp6_full_raster.log` is not given repo-relative. The probe bullet is also long for a Note.
issues.fix: Write 'the irispy 20210905 Si IV 1403 test fixture (187×40×29)' and `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_full_raster.log`. Cut the probe numbers to one sentence.

issues.problem: 'A threshold' has no default and no dialog field, and the done_when does not say what `rb_mask` holds where RB is NaN (masked pixels).
issues.fix: Make the threshold a dialog field with a stated, proposed default. Specify that `rb_mask` is 0 (or NaN) where RB is not finite.

issues.where: old_trace entry for the keyboard table (:495)
issues.problem: It says wp2-m3-calibrated-window-data 'also fixes the :495 wording', but the WP2 draft neither mentions :495 nor has that key.
issues.fix: Mark the :495 row as superseded by the restructured plan, with masks/quality in WP6 M2 and uncertainties in `wp2-m3-window-data`, or add a cross_wp_note asking WP2 to own the wording.

issues.problem: 'The docs build lists glue_solar.sources.fitting' is weaker than the WP2 standard ('Sphinx builds with -W').
issues.fix: Use: 'Sphinx builds with -W, the API page lists glue_solar.sources.fitting, and the page walks one Si IV fit…'.

### WP7: GOES and SDO context

Goal: on request, add the GOES XRS light curve and SDO/AIA pointing context for a loaded IRIS observation. WP7 reuses glue's Scatter, Image and Table viewers, `link_hpc` and datetime `Time` links, and adds no viewer. Primary paths: `glue_solar/sources/context.py` (new), registration in `glue_solar/__init__.py`, the gated datetime patch in `glue_solar/glue_patches.py`, the sunpy extra in `pyproject.toml`, and `glue_solar/tests/test_context.py`. User documentation belongs to WP9. Main has no GOES action today, and local co-aligned `aia_l2` cutouts already load through the browser. WP7 has no M0 or M1 work. M2 is done when a confirmed fetch that does not block the GUI produces two things. The first is a GOES light curve with correct date labels and a selected-exposure marker. The second is one AIA download that gives a full-disk locator and, when no cutout is loaded, an FOV crop. M3 adds the SWPC flare list, HCR metadata, and further AIA channels and HMI.

**Port from prototypes**

- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp7chk/context_chk.py` and `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp7chk/test_context.py` → `glue_solar/sources/context.py` and `glue_solar/tests/test_context.py`.

The tests are `test_setup_registers_context_actions`, `test_goes_xrs_reads_one_satellite`, `test_goes_xrs_without_data_raises`, the four `test_fov_polygon_*` cases, `test_aia_context_from_local_map`, `test_goes_context_shows_message_on_failure` and `test_sdo_context_end_to_end`. From `wp7_goes.py`, take only the viewer, log-axis and time-link recipe, not its `EPOCH=1` `rcParams['date.epoch']` path.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp0_bug_epoch_viewer.py` (kept as test evidence) → the 1.27.0 date-label assertion of `wp7-goes-date-labels` in `glue_solar/tests/test_context.py`. Archive it once that test exists.

**M2**

- [ ] **M2** `wp7-context-port`: Port the prototype into `glue_solar/sources/context.py` as two `menubar_plugin` actions, 'IRIS: GOES context…' and 'IRIS: SDO context…', imported by `glue_solar.setup()`. In `pyproject.toml`, change `sunpy[map,net]` to `sunpy[map,net,timeseries]` (the XRS reader needs cdflib and h5netcdf).

Run the search, download, file reads and AIA-only processing (corner transform, submap, resample) in glue-qt's `Worker`, as WP8's scan does. Create Data, links, subsets and viewers in the Worker's result slot. Every error becomes a message box.

**Notes and limits**

- **First exposure only.** The FOV outline and crop use the first exposure (frame or scan 0), and later pointing drift is not followed. The drift is 42.2 arcsec over 4.8 h on the 2021-09-05 irispy SJI fixture (OBSID 3620258102) (D1). The AIA context is the single image nearest STARTOBS, placed by header WCS and `link_hpc` only. No time series and no co-registration are claimed.
- **Not built:** new context viewers, cadence sync through spatial links, JSOC credentials, aiapy, a cross-correlation framework or an extra outline dataset. Time follows only through the `Time` links and the WP4 master-time marker.
- **Why SphericalScreen.** Without the screen, off-limb corners become NaN whenever the AIA observer or obstime differs from IRIS's, which is always the case for real AIA data. `submap` then raises.
- **GOES data.**
  - Sunpy 8.0.0 does not mask XRS quality flags.
  - SWPC publishes only the current primary satellite, so there is no rule for the historical "primary".
  - GOES 8–15 curves are unscaled science-quality data. SWPC and HEK flare classes use the old scale, so X1.0 is about 1.4e-4 W/m² on the curve.
  - GOES-19 needs sunpy 8.1 or later. The current primary is GOES-18 (SWPC instrument-sources.json, 2026-09-22), so this is not a gap today.
- **Marker export.** The marker is a matplotlib artist owned by the tool. It appears in 'Save plot to file' output but not in the Python-script export. The Line layers of glue #2603 and glue-qt #73 could replace it later.

### WP8: Browser, discovery and inputs

WP8 covers how IRIS files are found and turned into Glue datasets outside the quicklook preset: the observation browser (menubar 'IRIS: browse observations…', `QtIRISImporter`), the header scanner and the File→Open readers, in `glue_solar/sources/loaders/scan.py`, `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py`, `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris_loader.ui`, `glue_solar/sources/iris.py`, `glue_solar/conftest.py`, `glue_solar/tests/test_scan.py` and `glue_solar/tests/test_importer.py`. Done means: at M0 the browser lists and labels every file of the M0 acceptance observations correctly and the tests no longer write the user's settings; at M1 derived non-Level-2 files are never offered as rasters; at M2 the header scan runs in glue-qt's `Worker`, stops promptly and can be filtered; at M3 the browser adds time-window and date-tree search, `Fido` remote search, metadata tooltips and persisted settings, and File→Open reads Level-3 im files. Every item runs on released glue-core 1.27.0 / glue-qt 0.4.2 and needs no upstream PR.

Port from prototypes:
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp8_scan.py` → only the `stop` keyword of `scan_directory` and its poll (a 3-hunk diff against main), into `wp8-filter-stop`. First fix wp7-wp8-3 (poll during the directory walk, not after sorting) and rewrite the ported `test_scan_directory_stop_kwarg`, whose `len(polls) == 3` assumes one poll per sorted file. Port onto main after `wp8-sji-variants` and `wp8-derived-files`, so the prototype's stale copies of the TDESC1 keying (followup-4-5) and of the rb_steps acceptance (followup-4-6) do not come back.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp8_proto.py` + `wp8_loader.ui` → into `QtIRISImporter`: the `__init__` connections, `set_directory` (Worker, `_scan_id`, stop predicate), `_stop_scan`, `_scan_over`, `_scanned`, `_scan_failed`, `populate()` calling `_apply_filter`, `_apply_filter`, and the two .ui hunks (filterLayout; progressLayout with `stop_scan`). Drop the module-level `iris.UI_MAIN` override and `populate_threads`. First fix wp7-wp8-2, wp7-wp8-11 and wp7-wp8-3, add wp7-wp8-4 and wp7-wp8-13, and keep the `_scan_over` progress repair without resetting a completed extraction from 100 (archive-trace-16).
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp8_test_proto.py`, `wp8_test_shipped.py`, `wp8_chk_test_text.py` → into `test_scan.py`/`test_importer.py`: filter, rescan, stop keeps partial results, extraction text, close stops the scan, the `populates` fixture with its two tests, and the stop-message test (`ProtoImporter` case only). Add `qtbot.waitUntil(lambda: not dlg.scanning)` at the 10 sites in `test_importer.py` (as of main 236f0a8: constructions at 17/57/87/216/242, the recursive toggle at 78, finalize at 60/93/223/245). First fix wp7-wp8-12: gate on a `threading.Event`, not a 0.2 s sleep. Invert `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260927/test_v_wp8.py` tests f2/f3/f4/f11 into regressions that assert the fixed behaviour.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp8_chk_proto_fix.py` → comparison evidence only. It is the older variant (`setValue(0)` in `set_directory`, no repair in `_scan_over`) and on iris-plan does not break extraction-at-100. Archive it with `wp8_chk_test_text.py` once that test is ported without the parametrization.
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/review_20260905/qs_isolate.py` (loaded by `run_checks.py`) → not the runner: adapt only its `IsolatedQSettings` redirect into `glue_solar/conftest.py` as `wp8-test-qsettings`. This port is the fix for plan-integrity-2.

#### M0
- [ ] **M0** `wp8-test-qsettings`: Stop the test suite writing the user's settings. `QtIRISImporter.set_directory` writes `iris/last_dir` to the macOS domain `com.glue-solar.glue-solar` even with an isolated HOME (`loaders/iris.py:216-220`), and glue-qt's `get_qapp` saves `~/.glue/settings.cfg` when FONT_SIZE is unset (`glue_qt/utils/app.py:65-68`). In `glue_solar/conftest.py`, add a minimal `IsolatedQSettings` subclass adapted from `qs_isolate.py` (never imported) that maps the two-string constructor to IniFormat at `tmp_path / "glue-solar-glue-solar.ini"`, monkeypatch `glue_solar.sources.loaders.iris.QSettings` with it in an autouse fixture, and at conftest import point `glue.config.CFG_DIR` at a temporary directory as `glue_qt/conftest.py:63-66` does; until this lands every run uses `-p qs_isolate` with an isolated HOME. Done when a test asserts that `iris.QSettings('glue-solar', 'glue-solar').fileName()` lies under `tmp_path`, and after a plain `pytest glue_solar` run in the iris-plan env both `defaults read com.glue-solar.glue-solar` (macOS) and the mtime of `~/.glue/settings.cfg` are unchanged. Features: none (test infrastructure). Findings: plan-integrity-2.
- [ ] **M0** `wp8-sji-variants`: Key SJIs in `scan_directory` (`scan.py:165`) by TDESC1 plus the filename variant, e.g. 'SJI_2796 (deconvolved)' when `_deconvolved.` appears in the `strip_pooch` name; today a deconvolved file carries the plain TDESC1, sorts after the plain file and overwrites it. Pass the path into `_image_cube_data` (`loaders/iris.py:121-125`), called from `image_data`/`iris_data` (`:133-150`), so the browser and File→Open both label the dataset 'SJI_2796_deconvolved-<OBSID>-<STARTOBS>'. Done when:
  - CI: a new `tmp_path` test, following `test_load_selected_real_sji`, copies irispy's real `iris_l2_20210905_001833_3620258102_SJI_1400_t000` file twice, as `…_SJI_1400_t000.fits` and `…_SJI_1400_t000_deconvolved.fits`. The scan lists 'SJI_1400' and 'SJI_1400 (deconvolved)', both load through the dialog and through `read_iris_file`, and the two Data labels differ, the second naming the variant. `iris_tree` is not changed.
  - Local (skipped without ~/DATA/IRIS): the real 4000005156 `SJI_2796_t000_deconvolved.fits.gz` plus a symlink to it named without `_deconvolved` list and load as two entries, and every other observation's SJI, raster and window counts are unchanged.
  - No existing test fails or needs its assertions changed, so plain labels, colormaps and the (OBSID, STARTOBS to the second) grouping stay as they are. Features: F009. Findings: followup-4-5.

#### M1
- [ ] **M1** `wp8-derived-files`: In `_is_supported_file` (`scan.py:110-115`), accept an IRIS `SPEC` file only when its primary header has `DATA_LEV == 2`, without reading any extension. All 114 local Level-2 SPEC files and the irispy 0.9.0 fixtures carry it; the derived `iris_l2_20140910_fexxi_rb_steps` (PRIMARY/FEXXI_DATA/AUX, no TIME, no DATA_LEV/LVL_NUM/ENDOBS) does not and is offered today as an 'O I 1356' raster that fails to load. Skipped files are not listed and the progress text reports how many were skipped (default, confirm); a load failure names the file as well as the window (`finalize` names only the window today). In conftest, `_header` gains DATA_LEV=2; OBS_S stays stem-less as `{MD5}sparse_l2_raster.fits.gz` with DATA_LEV=2 and still no OBS_DESC/ENDOBS, so `_key_from_header` (`scan.py:153`) and `test_sparse_header_falls_back_to_obsid_description` keep their coverage; a new derived fixture takes the rb_steps name and layout (TELESCOP 'IRIS', INSTRUME 'SPEC', no DATA_LEV) with OBS_A's OBSID and STARTOBS. Done when:
  - On `iris_tree`, the derived fixture is never offered as a window, OBS_A keeps its 2 rasters (`a.nfiles == 4`), OBS_S is still found, the irispy Level-2 fixtures are still listed, and the progress text reports 1 skipped file.
  - `test_reader_failure_stays_in_dialog` asserts that the failing file's name appears in the message.
  - Local test (skipped without ~/DATA/IRIS): the scan finds 13 observations (14 today), skips 1 of the 130 FITS files, and no observation lists the rb_steps file. Features: none. Findings: followup-4-6.

#### M2
- [ ] **M2** `wp8-filter-stop`: Run `scan_directory` in glue-qt's `glue_qt.utils.threading.Worker` with a cooperative `stop` predicate, polled while the tree is enumerated (collect paths in a loop that breaks on `stop()`, then sort) and once per file, because `_stop_scan` calls `worker.wait()` on the GUI thread. Populate on the GUI thread, drop results with a stale scan id, and stop and await the previous worker on rescan, directory change, accept, reject and close. While a scan runs, disable Load and keep the archive-extraction messages; after a Stop, mark each possibly truncated observation '(partial scan)' and disable Stack for it, and show 'Scan stopped' only if the worker had not finished; `_scan_over` repairs an invalid progress value after `setRange(0, 100)` without resetting a completed extraction from 100 to 0. Done when:
  - Deterministic pytest-qt tests (fake header reads gated on a `threading.Event`, no sleeps) show that Stop or reject during a slowed walk returns after at most one further `is_file` call and within 0.5 s; Load during a gated rescan cannot load from the replaced list; after an early Stop an observation with 2 raster files shows 1 file and the partial marker; Stop after completion never shows 'Scan stopped'; stale scan ids are ignored; and the suite passes 20 consecutive runs.
  - Local on ~/DATA/IRIS (13 observations): GUI timer gaps stay ≤ 0.2 s during the scan and header reads have a median ≤ 5 ms/file. Features: F005. Findings: wp7-wp8-2, wp7-wp8-3, wp7-wp8-4, wp7-wp8-11, wp7-wp8-12, archive-trace-16, followup-2-8 (WP8 thresholds only). Depends: wp8-sji-variants, wp8-derived-files, wp8-test-qsettings; rebase onto wp10-nonblocking-load's Worker, stale-id and busy-state handling in the same dialog.
- [ ] **M2** `wp8-text-filter`: Add one case-insensitive `filter` QLineEdit to `iris_loader.ui` that matches STARTOBS, OBSID, description, and the window, SJI and AIA names in child rows (column 6 for single-entry rows). ISO date substrings give day, month and year filtering; a pre-scan time search is `wp8-prescan-search`. The filter survives rescans, hidden ticked items still load, Load shows how many ticked items are hidden, and the object names `filter`, `stop_scan` and `progress` are kept. Done when on `iris_tree` 'mg ii' keeps only OBS_A and shows its Mg II child row, '2023-02' keeps only OBS_B, a hidden ticked observation makes Load read e.g. 'Load selected (1 hidden)' and still loads, and the filter text survives a rescan. Features: none (usability; date substrings partly serve F001). Findings: wp7-wp8-13. Depends: wp8-filter-stop.

#### M3
- [ ] **M3** `wp8-prescan-search`: Add keyword-only `start`, `stop`, `glob`, `date_tree`, `max_duration` (default 1 day) and `first_raster_header_only=False` arguments to `scan_directory`, pruning before any header read:
  - in window or date-tree mode, skip files whose `_key_from_name` stamp lies outside [start − max_duration, stop], and count unstamped files as skipped without reading them;
  - apply the `fnmatch` glob to `strip_pooch(name)`;
  - in date-tree mode, descend only into YYYY/MM/DD directories inside that interval;
  - after reading, keep only observations with STARTOBS ≤ stop and ENDOBS ≥ start;
  - with `first_raster_header_only=True`, append further `_raster_t###_r#####` files of an observation keyed by filename without reading their headers (the iris_xfiles one-header-per-group speed-up); `QtIRISImporter` passes True (default, confirm).

  Add `find_observation_files(time, root, sji=False, nearest=False)` over `scan_directory`, returning the raster repeats (or with `sji=True` the SJIs) of the observation covering `time`, with `nearest` falling back to the closest observation (iris_find_file parity). Done when tests that count `fits.getheader` calls, on a temporary YYYY/MM/DD symlink tree of real ~/DATA/IRIS files (local) with a CI variant on `iris_tree`, show:
  - a 2013-09-02 window reads only headers stamped 2013-09-01 to 2013-09-02 and lists only 4000255147 and 4000005156, and date-tree mode never enters a directory outside the interval;
  - `glob='iris_l2_2025*'` lists only 3400109360 and 3893010094, excluding the 3640107442 AIA cutouts;
  - `find_observation_files('2013-09-02T17:00', root)` returns the 4000255147 raster and with `sji=True` its SJI_1400 (that observation runs 16:39:35 to 17:58:48, so pruning must keep it), and `nearest=True` on an uncovered time returns the closest observation;
  - `first_raster_header_only=True` reads 1 SPEC header for 3602506433 (99 rasters, local) and for OBS_A (2 rasters, CI) and still lists every raster and the same windows;
  - with no new arguments, results equal today's scan. Features: F003, F010. Findings: wp7-wp8-10. Depends: wp8-filter-stop.
- [ ] **M3** `wp8-search-ui`: In `QtIRISImporter`/`iris_loader.ui`, add Start and Stop UTC `QDateTimeEdit` fields with 'Last 5 days' and 'Up until now' presets and an 'Ignore times' toggle; user-defined named search locations (name → root, date tree, search subfolders, glob) chosen from a combo and shipped with one 'local' default, IDL's free/LMSAL/UIO presets being added only with roots copied from and cited to iris_xfiles source; and a 'Recent searches' list of the last 10 windows. Store them in the existing `QSettings('glue-solar', 'glue-solar')` store beside `iris/last_dir` (`loaders/iris.py:24-25,128-130`) and pass every value to the `wp8-prescan-search` arguments. Done when pytest-qt with isolated QSettings shows that 'Last 5 days' sets Start to now − 5 d and Stop to now; 'Ignore times' gives the same result as an unwindowed scan; a location can be added, edited and removed, and restores its root, date-tree, subfolder and glob values after reopening; and the recent list stops at 10 with a chosen entry restoring Start/Stop. Features: F001, F002, F004. Depends: wp8-prescan-search, wp8-test-qsettings.
- [ ] **M3** `wp8-browser-conveniences`: Persist the 'Search subfolders' and 'Stack' checkboxes and the filter text in the same QSettings store. Make the Folder QLineEdit editable (readOnly at `iris_loader.ui:27-30`) and rescan on `editingFinished`. Double-clicking a checkable leaf or a single-entry observation row loads only that payload and leaves other ticks untouched (`finalize` today loads every ticked row); a multi-entry parent row keeps Qt's expand/collapse. Record each dataset's source path(s) in `data.meta['SOURCE_FILES']` inside `raster_data`, `image_data` and `iris_data`, which the `wp3-file-references` factories (`read_iris_rasters`, `read_iris_image`) call, so both load routes set it and glue-qt's 'View metadata/header' and the IPython terminal show it; the key is display-only provenance, and sessions relocate files through the WP3 `load_data`/LoadLog route. Done when pytest-qt with isolated QSettings shows that values set before closing are restored on reopen; typing a path and pressing Enter rescans, while an invalid path shows a message and keeps the list; with another row ticked, double-clicking a leaf or single-entry row loads only it and double-clicking a parent row only expands or collapses it; and a loaded SJI stores its absolute path in `meta['SOURCE_FILES']`, OBS_A's two-raster stack stores both paths, and `MetadataDialog` lists them. Features: F006, F007, F014. Depends: wp8-text-filter, wp8-test-qsettings, wp3-file-references.
- [ ] **M3** `wp8-browser-metadata`: Add tooltips, not columns, to observation rows and window/SJI items, filled from the primary headers `scan.py` already reads and stored on `Observation` at scan time: TWMINn/TWMAXn/TDETn and window size from TSCn/TECn/TSRn/TERn; NRASTERP, FOVX/FOVY and STEPT_AV; binning from SUMSPTRF/SUMSPTRN/SUMSPAT (SUMSPAT for the spatial bin, not copying the IDL SPATIAL BIN label bug); OBSLABEL/OBSTITLE and the ObsID decoding `scan.py` already does. No extra header reads and no OBS XML. Done when on the irispy 20140329 fixture raster the C II window tooltip starts 'C II 1336: 1332.73–1337.22 Å, FUV1'; on the local 2013, 2014 and 2018 observations every tooltip number equals that file's header value (e.g. 3824262996 C II 1336 = 1332.70–1337.58 Å); and the scan tests' counted header reads are unchanged. Features: F039, F040.
- [ ] **M3** `wp8-remote-search`: Build remote discovery on `sunpy.net.Fido` (glue-solar already requires `sunpy[net]`) as a `menubar_plugin` 'IRIS: search online…' that calls `Fido.search(a.Time(...), a.Instrument('IRIS'))` (verified 2026-09-27: VSO returns per-observation Level-2 records from provider LMSAL, including per-channel SJIs, deconvolved variants and the raster archive), filters the results by the OBSID in `fileid`, fetches the ticked rows with `Fido.fetch` in the existing `Worker` into a chosen folder, and opens `QtIRISImporter` there, which already extracts raster `.tar.gz` files. Do not rebuild the LMSAL search page (FOV/cadence/target filters, AIA footprints, preview movies); link to it from the dialog. Done when mocked-network tests show results grouped by observation, a working OBSID filter, no network work on Cancel, and an unchanged folder and data collection after a fetch error; the dialog shows a clickable link to the LMSAL IRIS search page whose URL is checked by hand in a browser before merge; and an opt-in network test (skipped by default) downloads the ~39 MB SJI_1400 record of the 2021-04-29 observation 3660259102, which the browser then lists under that observation. Features: F016, F017, F018. Depends: wp8-filter-stop.
- [ ] **M3** `wp8-m3-level3-input`: Register a glue-solar `data_factory` 'IRIS Level 3 FITS' in `glue_solar/sources/iris.py`, following `read_iris_file`, whose identifier accepts a `*_im.fits` name with the three Level-3 extensions at priority 210, above `is_iris_fits`, which claims every TELESCOP 'IRIS' file at 200 (add a header-keyword test once a real file confirms one). The reader reads the im cube (x, y, wave, time) with `astropy.io.fits`; takes wavelengths from extension 1; converts extension-2 times (seconds since DATE_OBS, shape (nx, ntime)) into a datetime64 `Time` component broadcast as at `loaders/iris.py:81-84`; turns extension-3 slit positions into components; and builds the spatial WCS from the header, where VER_RF3 (the iris_xfiles r1.41 cutoff) selects which exposure time CRVALn refers to. Transposed sp files are not claimed, and Level-3 writing stays a permanent non-goal. Done when synthetic ITN26-layout im files with VER_RF3 on each side of the cutoff each load through the Level-3 factory as one Data whose wavelengths match extension 1, whose `Time` equals DATE_OBS + extension 2 and whose spatial WCS matches the header at the exposure VER_RF3 selects, and the Level-2 fixtures and irispy files are not claimed by the Level-3 factory. Features: F025.

Notes and limits:
- The M2 port makes the scan non-blocking and stoppable but still reads every supported FITS header; `first_raster_header_only` (M3) is the speed-up. On ~/DATA/IRIS, 130 header reads take 0.49 s in total (median 0.8 ms, max 165.6 ms on the 67 MB SJI .fits.gz), so stop latency is bounded by one header read. The capability row is 'Observation browsing: filter and stop' (wp7-wp8-10).
- The scan Worker reads only primary headers and never touches QSettings or widgets. Loading datasets off the GUI thread is wp10-nonblocking-load (followup-2-9), which builds Data in the worker, adds it on the GUI thread and never touches a viewer-held -TAB WCS (followup-2-1).
- Deconvolved SJIs are recognised by filename only: plain and deconvolved headers are identical (no DECON keyword), so a deconvolved file renamed without `_deconvolved` cannot be told apart.
- `QtIRISImporter.finalize`, `iris_loader.ui` and `test_importer.py` are also edited by WP3 (`wp3-file-references`, M1: loads through `load_data(..., factory=...)`), WP4 (`wp4-launch-preset`: 'Open quicklook' option and per-dataset observation record), WP10 (`wp10-nonblocking-load`) and WP1. Land WP8 M2 after those and rebase its test waits onto them; WP8 M2 needs no other M2 package.
- Kept non-goals: no OBS XML viewer or resolver, no pipeline-log viewer (reconsider only for a concrete pipeline-mirror request), no EIS sources (F019), no Level-3 writing, no rebuild of the LMSAL search page, and no new dependency.
- Still unverified: `Fido` downloads end to end and the LMSAL search-page URL (iris.lmsal.com returned 403); the Level-3 header keyword and the exact VER_RF3 mapping (read them from iris_xfiles / `iris_make_fits_level3` source before implementing, and retest on a real iris_xfiles Level-3 file when one is obtained; none exists locally); IDL location roots; date-tree pruning on a real LMSAL or UiO mirror.

final.markdown:
### WP10: Loader robustness and performance

WP10 makes the IRIS loaders correct and fast enough for the M0 quicklook on real data, and later lazy enough for larger observations. Primary paths: `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py` (`_cube_data`, `_GlueWCS`, `raster_data`, `QtIRISImporter.finalize`), `glue_solar/sources/loaders/stack_spectrograms.py`, the WP4 preset module `glue_solar/quicklook.py`, `glue_solar/tests/test_importer.py` and a data-gated `glue_solar/tests/test_performance.py`. M0 is done when the M0 blockers are fixed on glue-core 1.27.0, glue-qt 0.4.2 and irispy 0.9.0 (fill values stored as NaN, uint8 masks, negative-step rasters, the WCS thread crash, the large-data modal, the -TAB slider latency and the raster-ROI guard) and the `wp10-m0-acceptance` budgets pass on the named data. M1 moves loading off the GUI thread and makes raster ROIs cheap on SJIs, M2 adds lazy memmap/dask access, and M3 adds sit-and-stare chunks only if the measurements call for them. Non-blocking load is M1, not M0, because it is not on the M0 blocker list (default, confirm; effort M, feasible on released glue-qt). Until then each ticked pick freezes the GUI for 1.0-3.1 s (2.7 s for the 4000255147 SJI 1400 `.fits.gz`, 3.1 s for a 50-scan stack).

Port from prototypes:
- `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp8_proto.py`, `IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp8_scan.py` → only the pattern for `wp10-nonblocking-load` (the code ports under WP8 `wp8-filter-stop`): a `Worker`, an id that drops stale results and a `stop()` poll per file; build the Data in the worker, add it on the GUI thread, never touch viewer-held WCS objects from the worker. Fix first: no `wait()` on the GUI thread (wp7-wp8-3), and OK stays disabled while a scan or load runs (wp7-wp8-2).

- [ ] **M0** `wp10-fill-nan`: In `_cube_data` (`glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:72-85`), replace IRIS missing samples with NaN (D12): detect `np.isin(values, (-200, -199))` on the already-flipped data, never irispy's `cube.mask` (built before the STEPS_AV < -0.01 flip, `irispy/io/spectrograph.py:251@0.9.0`), and convert with `astype(np.result_type(dtype, np.float32), copy=False)` only when a fill value is present. AIA cutouts (TDESC1 not starting with 'SJI', the `_image_cube_data` check at `iris.py:122-124`) treat only -200 as missing, and saturation (+Inf, the int16 16182 DN top code) is left unchanged. `stack_spectrograms.py` fills each scan as it writes it into the memmap (dropping the mask `.copy()` at :54-56 and `mask=~np.isfinite(output)` at :79), and `_raster_collection_data` calls `_cube_data` for the stack with the fill step skipped; update `test_importer.py:175` and `:180` to the fill-derived rule and `isnan`. Done when:
  - CI: `raster_data` on the irispy fixture `iris_l2_20210905_001833_3620258102_raster_t000_r00000_test.fits` Si IV 1403 gives 0 values of -200/-199 and exactly 35,027 NaN of 216,920 samples; a synthetic negative-step fixture (flipped data, unflipped irispy mask) gets NaN exactly at the flipped fill positions.
  - 4000005156 Si IV scan 0 has no -200/-199 and a NaN count equal to the raw count of those codes (today 3,050,445 values of -200 and 0 NaN); the default percentile lower limit is no longer -200 and the per-scan and stack limits agree; a one-pixel Pixel-subset Mean spectrum equals the raw spectrum with fill set to NaN, so the dataset's Mean profile gets no fill contribution.
  - On 3400109360 the NaN positions of each scan and of the 2-scan stack equal the flipped raw fill positions. Today scan 0 C II's mask differs from the flipped fill at 7026 pixels, and the 2-scan stack has 62,022 NaNs at wrong positions and 62,022 fill values kept as data.
  - A synthetic int16 AIA-like cutout with injected -200 renders those pixels transparent (#53) and a fill-free cutout stays int16 (no local cutout contains -200).

  Features: F164, F031. Findings: followup-3-3, followup-4-2, followup-3-2.
- [ ] **M0** `wp10-mask-uint8`: In `_cube_data`, after the fill step, store the mask of every SJI, per-scan and stack dataset as `Component(np.isnan(values).view(np.uint8))`, holding no second in-RAM copy (glue's `coerce_numeric` stores bool as int64 and keeps uint8). Done when every mask component is uint8 and equals `isnan(data)` (on real SJIs: `cube.mask` plus the -199 pixels), with the `test_importer.py:109-112, 136, 171-180` assertions updated; on the 24 GB reference machine `raster_data` on all 9 windows of 4000005156 scan 0 retains ≤ 6 B/element and peaks at ≤ 10 B/element, and stacking all 7 windows of the 99-scan 3602506433 peaks below 12 GB (50 scans measured 10.07 GB; 99 untested). If these hold, lazy loading stays in M2. Features: none. Findings: followup-2-2, usefulness-12. Depends: wp10-fill-nan.
- [ ] **M0** `wp10-m0-negative-step`: In `_cube_data`, when the header has STEPS_AV < -0.01 and the probe `abs(Tx[0] - lon(step 0)) > abs(Tx[-1] - lon(step 0))` fires (Tx = the x of `meta['exposure FOV center']`, lon = WCS longitude at the FOV-centre slit row), assign `data.meta` a copy of `cube.meta` in which the step-axis arrays of the five irispy per-step keys (auxiliary times, exposure time, exposure FOV center, observer radial velocity, orbital phase) are reversed; never modify `cube.meta` in place. This keeps irispy's default orientation (D10); mask and NaN already follow the flipped data through `wp10-fill-nan`. Remove it once an irispy release flips the mask, uncertainty and meta (WP0), at which point the probe stops firing. Done when:
  - The probe fires for both 3400109360 scans and not for 4000005156, 4000255147 or 3824262996.
  - On a synthetic negative-step raster with varying exposure times, `data.meta['exposure time'][k]` equals the file's EXPTIMEF at row N-1-k (3400109360 itself is constant at 7.999 s).
  - WP4's nearest-index arrays on a 3400109360 scan and on its 2-scan stack match a brute-force nearest search over the descending `Time`, with ties resolved to the earlier time (D7) and duplicate times to the first index (D10).
  - SJI slit and marker positions on descending-step scans are recorded as untested until a 3400109360 SJI has been fetched with the user's approval.

  Features: none. Findings: followup-4-2. Depends: wp10-fill-nan, wp4-time-sync (nearest-index check only).
- [ ] **M0** `wp10-m0-wcs-lock`: Serialize `_GlueWCS.pixel_to_world_values`, `world_to_pixel_values` and `axis_correlation_matrix` (`glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py`) with one module-level `threading.RLock`: re-entrant because a `_GlueWCS` can wrap a sliced `_GlueWCS`, module-level because derived datasets share one astropy WCS. Keep the lock until an astropy release fixes astropy#19174 (WP0). Done when a CI subprocess test exits 0 with two threads each making 20,000 calls on one `_GlueWCS` of the bundled irispy raster fixture (unpatched: crashed 5/5; the test takes 6.7 s), and each real-data scenario runs 20 consecutive offscreen times with 0 crashes: (a) the quicklook on 3824262996 Mg II k (2.35e8 elements) with 3 Pixel clicks; (b) 4000255147 Si IV in stock viewers (2 Image, 1 Profile), stepping the slice from 100 to 300 (today 4 of 8 threaded runs crash). If (b) still crashes with the lock, find the remaining shared state before M0 closes. Features: none. Findings: followup-2-1, followup-3-1. Depends: wp4-quicklook-preset (scenario a only; the CI test and scenario b can land first).
- [ ] **M0** `wp10-m0-interaction-latency`: Add `_without_step_index(wcs)` to `loaders/iris.py` and call it in `_cube_data` before wrapping and on `target_wcs` at `stack_spectrograms.py:36`. For an `astropy.wcs.WCS` whose -TAB table carries the exposure-index column (`PS3_2 = 'RASTER'`, `irispy/io/spectrograph.py:79-108@0.9.0`) it rebuilds the WCS from `to_header()` without `PS3_2` plus a 2-node index, and uses the rebuilt WCS only if both agree to 1e-12 at probe points, otherwise it keeps the original and logs it. It is a no-op for the SJI gWCS and for WCSes without an index column, so it retires itself once an irispy release drops the index (WP0). Keep λ–t as an Image axis choice (`glue/viewers/image/state.py:326-349@1.27.0`) with no transposed cube; if a budget still fails, set `QSlider.setTracking(False)` on the preset's `value_slice_center` sliders (`glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.ui:88@0.4.2`) instead of adding a cache, and consider a numpy slit-table evaluator only if a budget then still fails. Done when:
  - On 4000255147 Si IV a spectrogram slice step (set + draw) takes ≤ 0.10 s and stays within 20% across exposures 1, 800 and 1599 (unfixed 0.059 → 0.226 s, fixed 0.057-0.064 s).
  - The rebuilt WCS matches the original to 1e-12 deg (pixel→world) and 1e-9 px (world→pixel) at the far slit end and at fractional steps on 4000255147, 4000005156 and 3824262996.
  - The λ–t image at the selected point equals `cube[:, y, :]`.
  - The existing SJI tests in `test_importer.py` pass unchanged and SJI coords still wrap the gWCS.

  Features: F035, F022. Findings: followup-2-6. Depends: wp10-m0-wcs-lock.
- [ ] **M0** `wp10-m0-large-data-modal`: In the WP4 preset (`glue_solar/quicklook.py`), create the Profile viewer without data, set `large_data_size = None` on that instance (glue reads the instance attribute, `glue/viewers/common/viewer.py:200@1.27.0`), then call `add_data`, so the 1e8-point 'Add large data set?' modal (default Cancel) cannot abort the preset. Show the data size as a non-blocking status-bar note; if `profile.add_data` returns False, show the reason in the status bar and continue without the Profile layer. User settings and the class attribute stay unchanged. Done when, at real size and without monkeypatching `warn`, the preset opens with the Profile layer and `warn` is never called on the 4000255147 sit-and-stare windows (1.7e8-3.7e8 elements), 3824262996 Mg II k (2.35e8) and the 99-scan 3602506433 stack (4.6e8). Features: none. Findings: followup-2-5, usefulness-12. Depends: wp4-quicklook-preset.
