Notes and limits:
- Stack storage stays as on main: the optional 4D stack is a temp-file floating memmap of `np.result_type(first scan, float32)` (float32 for the tested IRIS arrays, not a universal cast) with NaN at missing samples, using scan 0's nominal spatial WCS without resampling (per-scan WCS is `wp1-stack-per-scan-wcs`); load scans separately for their distinct pointings. `irispy.io.read_files` still reads the files; glue-solar only replaces -200/-199 with NaN, reverses negative-step per-step meta and drops the -TAB step index. Unstacked datasets keep detector arrays, uint8 masks, metadata, units, WCS and exact exposure times.
- The fill rule matches exact codes, not IRIS-SSW's `< -198.5`, because the irispy float fixtures hold genuine values below -200; -199 is unverified for AIA, so AIA uses -200 only; the int16 16182 DN top code is kept, as in Level-3 and CRISPEX. After `wp10-fill-nan` downstream code must handle NaN, notably the WP2 moments and the WP6 fits (`IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp6_fitting.py:61` uses `nan_to_num`). The in-place write (`copy=False`) changes irispy's cube array, which is safe while the loader discards the cube.
- Why the lock: glue-qt 0.4.2 computes Profile layers above 1e7 elements in a worker (`glue_qt/viewers/profile/layer_artist.py:50@0.4.2`) and the histogram viewer is threaded, while WCSAxes calls the same irispy -TAB WCS on the GUI thread, and wcslib `tabx2s` writes shared scratch fields with the GIL released (astropy#19174). The lock covers only calls through `_GlueWCS`: code that uses the raw astropy WCS (`data.coords._wcs` in the WP2 and WP6 prototypes, `SlicedLowLevelWCS(raw_wcs)` in the WP6 worker) must go through `data.coords` or use its own deep copy. Other WCS attribute reads stay unlocked; none crashed in 18 locked runs. Run crash tests only in a subprocess.
- Why the step index is slow: wcslib searches the explicit identity index column linearly (astropy `cextern/wcslib/C/tab.c:1169`, `:1209`), so the per-point cost grows with the exposure index. Raster world→pixel through `tabs2x` stays slow with or without the index (31 µs/pt on the 400-step raster, about 7 ms/pt on sit-and-stare), so any later design that maps many SJI points to raster pixels needs an analytic inverse; single-point lookups are fine. A numpy slit-table evaluator measured exact to 1e-10 arcsec at 0.07-0.08 s per step.
- Stock paths outside the preset behave as stock in M0: the ImageViewer's 'profile-viewer' tool opens a stock Profile viewer with the modal, and after Cancel there the closed viewer's `LayerArtistView` stays subscribed so every later `new_data_viewer` raises (WP0 reports this); raster ROIs in stock viewers cost about 10 s per SJI frame until `wp10-m1-roi-world-polygon`; histogram viewers warn at 2e7 points.
- Timings were taken offscreen with Agg under a load average of 3-11 from other jobs; on-screen Qt, cold-cache and network-drive loads are unmeasured, and the data tier cannot run in CI. For scale, uint8 masks took 4000005156 scan 0 (all 9 windows) from 8 to 1 B/element of mask and maxrss from 2.01 to 1.32 GB. Upstream fixes that retire the workarounds are tracked in WP0: the irispy index column and V34 flip, and astropy#19174.

Their headroom over the review's measurements is 1.5-1.9x (image step 0.10 vs 0.057-0.064 s, λ–t 0.15 vs 0.08-0.09 s, Pixel click 0.35 vs 0.219 s, SJI step 0.15 vs 0.10 s), and only 1.14x for the synced step (0.25 vs an unverified ~0.22 s estimate). The disposition asked for pass/fail budgets.
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The budgets are fixed pass/fail values with 1.5-1.9x headroom over the review's offscreen measurements. The synced-step budget rests on an unverified 0.22 s estimate. A budget changes only through a recorded decision after the first run, never automatically.' Also start the checkbox with an imperative ('Add a two-tier pass/fail gate ...'), as the format requires.

issues.problem: The probe abs(Tx[0]-lon(step 0)) > abs(Tx[-1]-lon(step 0)) runs on every raster, and the text does not say where lon is evaluated. On a sit-and-stare with little pointing drift (4000255147, STEPS_AV 0), both sides are close to 0 and noise can trigger the probe, which would then reverse the meta of a raster irispy never flipped. The Done when tests only 3400109360 (fires) and 4000005156 (does not fire).
issues.fix: Switch the reversal on only when the header has STEPS_AV < -0.01 AND the probe fires, with lon evaluated at the FOV-centre slit row. STEPS_AV is a data property, not a version, so D2 still holds. Add 4000255147 and 3824262996 to the 'probe does not fire' datasets.

issues.where: wp10-m0-negative-step, 'reverses the per-step meta that it publishes itself: exposure time, XCENIX/YCENIX, OBS_VRIX and OPHASEIX'
issues.problem: glue-solar does not publish these arrays separately. `_cube_data` sets `data.meta = cube.meta` (iris.py:76), and the stack uses `dict(cube_sequence[0].meta)`. So the per-step arrays are irispy's SGMeta entries 'auxiliary times', 'exposure time', 'exposure FOV center', 'observer radial velocity' and 'orbital phase' (irispy 0.9.0 io/spectrograph.py:210-230). The list leaves out 'auxiliary times', which is also unflipped, and names aux-table columns rather than the keys that reach glue. It also does not say whether the reversal happens in place.
issues.fix: Reword to: 'When the probe fires, assign data.meta a copy of cube.meta in which the step-axis arrays of the five irispy per-step keys (auxiliary times, exposure time, exposure FOV center, observer radial velocity, orbital phase) are reversed; never modify cube.meta in place.' Make the synthetic Done when test data.meta['exposure time'][k] against the file's EXPTIMEF at row N-1-k.

issues.where: wp10-fill-nan, Done when, fourth bullet ('Today each scan has 7026 mismatches')
issues.problem: This misstates the evidence. The 7026 figure is the mismatch between irispy's mask (and today's int64 mask component) and data == -200 on 3400109360 scan 0 C II (r00000) only. Per-scan data contains no NaN today. The stack measured 62,022 wrong NaNs plus 62,022 -200 values kept as data.
issues.fix: Write: 'Today scan 0 C II's mask differs from the flipped fill at 7026 pixels, and the 2-scan stack has 62,022 NaNs at wrong positions and 62,022 fill values kept as data.'

issues.where: wp10-m0-acceptance CI tier, and wp10-fill-nan Done when

final.markdown:
### WP11: Display, readouts and inspection tools

WP11 brings CRISPEX-level display and inspection to stock Glue Image and Profile viewers. It adds no viewer or renderer. Everything goes through public registries in glue-solar's `setup()` (`viewer_tool`, `stretches`, `keyboard_shortcut`, loader styles), plus one dock widget. The one exception is the gated, registered private aspect patch (D2). Primary paths are `glue_solar/tools.py`, `glue_solar/__init__.py`, `glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py` and `glue_solar/sources/loaders/stack_spectrograms.py`. The baseline is already on `main` (#52/#53): image sliders and playback, alpha/mix, the `solar:frame_time` label, the `solar:cursor_readout` position/value readout (registered only while glue-qt lacks `cursor_status`) and transparent NaN pixels. What 'done' means at each milestone:
- **M0:** the readout no longer shares the Pixel tool's icon.
- **M1:** labelled readouts with hover time and exposure, a selected-point panel, IRIS scaling (histogram-opt, gamma, per-frame limits, raster colour tables), physical raster aspect and navigation keys.
- **M2:** colour bar, distance and zoom tools.
- **M3:** optional conveniences.

#### M0

- [ ] **M0** `wp11-readout-icon`: Give `solar:cursor_readout` its own icon in `glue_solar/tools.py`. On released glue-qt 0.4.2 it sits next to glue's Pixel tool (`image:point_selection`), and both use `glue_crosshair` (tools.py:81@236f0a8; pixel_selection_mode.py:18@1.27.0). Change `docs/user_guide/guide-to-glue-1dprofile-viewer-for-iris-data.rst:54` to call the Pixel tool by its 'Pixel' label instead of 'the crosshair icon'. Done when: on released glue-qt 0.4.2, an Image viewer shows different icons for 'Pixel' and 'Cursor readout', and the guide no longer mentions a crosshair icon. Features: none. Findings: solar-main-3.

#### M1

- [ ] **M1** `wp11-cursor-readout`: Split `CursorReadoutTool` (glue_solar/tools.py:69-127@236f0a8) so that a glue-qt release with Qt #74 does not remove the IRIS readout. Add no new tool or icon.
  - Generic part, still gated on glue-qt lacking `cursor_status`: show the pixel and world position together, then the value. Build the text from `data.coords.pixel_to_world_values` at the full index (x, y and the viewer's current slices), not from `axes.format_coord`. Label the axes `Solar X` then `Solar Y` in arcsec to 0.01″ at any zoom, and give λ in Å. A `ProfileViewer` branch under the same gate shows x from `event.xdata` in the display unit, and y.
  - IRIS part, in the existing always-registered `solar:frame_time` label: while the mouse is over the axes, show the `Time` and `Exposure time` at the hovered pixel. A raster map therefore shows each step's own UTC (CRISPEX 'Local' time). Add km/s when `meta.get("rest_wavelength")` exists; that is the WP5 key, never irispy's `rest_wavelength` property, which returns TWAVE (D11). Otherwise the label shows the displayed frame or range.

  Done when:
  - On the local 4000005156 Si IV scan-0 raster map, hovering step s shows Solar X/Y equal to `pixel_to_world_values` to 0.01″ at two zoom levels, and λ in Å. The frame_time label shows step s's UTC (within 1 ms of irispy's time extra coord) and its exposure, and leaving the axes restores the frame range.
  - On 4000255147 SJI_1400 the label shows the displayed frame's time. Data without `Time` shows no time, and km/s appears only with a rest wavelength.
  - A Profile viewer of a raster spectrum reads x in Å, and in km/s once `wp5-m1-velocity-axis` provides that unit.
  - With `ImageViewer.cursor_status` monkeypatched in, the gated tool is absent and the frame_time label still shows the hover time and exposure.

  Features: F100, F101, F113. Findings: followup-3-10, followup-3-11. Depends: wp4-exposure-readout, wp10-m0-wcs-lock, wp5-m1-rest-wavelength-policy (km/s only).
- [ ] **M1** `wp11-selected-point-panel`: Add the CRISPEX parameter-overview equivalent as a read-only dock widget. A glue-solar `viewer_tool` toggles it and the quicklook opens it; the control-panel clone stays a non-goal. The panel listens to `SubsetUpdateMessage` for the active Pixel `PixelSubsetState`. For each dataset in the tab it lists pixel indices, Solar X/Y [arcsec], λ [Å] with its index, km/s (only with `meta.get("rest_wavelength")`), scan/step, SJI frame, UTC, exposure duration and value. Below the rows it shows the WP4 master and the signed SJI–raster offset, or 'no match'. `PixelSubsetState` fixes only the two clicked axes (pixel_selection_subset_state.py:30-57@1.27.0). All other indices come from the viewers' `state.slices` as the WP4 controllers set them, so the panel adds no coordination logic. Fields persist when the mouse leaves. Done when:
  - CI on the irispy 0.9.0 20140329 3860258481 raster (one scan as 3D, all scans as 4D), after a Pixel click:
    - each field equals a direct read at the same indices (arcsec from `pixel_to_world_values`, UTC from `Time`, duration from `Exposure time`, value from `data[...]`);
    - the fields persist after the mouse moves;
    - closing the quicklook removes the panel and disconnects its callbacks;
    - paired with the unrelated 3880012095 SJI_1400 fixture, the SJI row shows 'no match'.
  - Real run on local 4000255147 + SJI_1400: the SJI frame row equals WP4's nearest exposure, and switching the master shows the signed offset per D7.
  - Sub-check, closed with `wp1-m1-sji-to-raster`: a point clicked on the SJI fills the raster rows, and a point clicked on the raster fills the SJI rows.

  Features: F099, F191. Findings: plan-integrity-22, core-qt-capabilities-1. Depends: wp4-quicklook-preset, wp4-m0-point-fixed-index, wp4-time-sync, wp4-exposure-readout, wp1-m1-wrapper-coherence.
- [ ] **M1** `wp11-histo-opt-scaling`: Add a glue-solar 'Scaling' `viewer_tool` menu (`Tool.menu_actions`) for Image viewers.
  - 'Histogram opt' takes a cutoff c of 1e-2, 1e-3 (the IRIS_HISTO_OPT default) or 1e-4 (the CRISPEX default). It sets the reference layer's `v_min`/`v_max` to `np.nanpercentile(layer_state.get_sliced_data(), [100·c, 100·(1−c)])`, which works per displayed slice as IRIS_HISTO_OPT does. Glue shows the result as 'Custom'.
  - 'Follow frames' re-applies these limits whenever `viewer_state.slices` changes.
  - 'Per-frame auto limits' toggles `stretch_global`, which has no glue-qt control.

  Add no percentile choices: a restored session rejects them (`ValueError value 99.8 is not in valid choices`). The M1 quicklook preset calls the same helper. Done when:
  - on local 3610108077 after `wp10-fill-nan`, cutoff 1e-3 gives limits equal to the displayed slice's nanpercentiles at 0.1 and 99.9, with v_min > −200;
  - with 'Follow frames' on, a wavelength step moves the limits to the new slice's percentiles;
  - toggling per-frame limits makes stock percentile limits change with the slider;
  - a saved session restores the Custom limits.

  Features: F061, F064. Findings: followup-3-4, followup-3-2. Depends: wp10-fill-nan.
- [ ] **M1** `wp11-gamma-stretch`: In `setup()`, register fixed-exponent gamma stretches through `glue.config.stretches.add`, with the display names 'Gamma 0.4', 'Gamma 0.75', 'Gamma 1.5' and 'Gamma 2.2'. Each is a no-argument astropy `PowerStretch` subclass, and labels that are already registered are skipped. 0.75 is IRIS_INTSCALE's SJI 2796 exponent, and sqrt already covers γ = 0.5. CRISPEX applies γ to the scaled data, which `PowerStretch` reproduces. Done when:
  - 'Gamma 0.75' is listed in the Stretch combo on released glue-qt 0.4.2;
  - its rendered normalised values equal `PowerStretch(0.75)` of the linear ones;
  - a session using it restores;
  - calling `setup()` twice raises nothing;
  - the IRIS-9 'gamma < 1' step works in the preset.

  Features: F062. Findings: usefulness-17, followup-3-4.
- [ ] **M1** `wp11-raster-cmap`: In `_raster_collection_data` (glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:104-118@main), pass `cmap=` to `_cube_data` for per-scan rasters and stacks. Use 'irissjiFUV' or 'irissjiNUV', chosen from each window's `SGMeta.detector_band`, which reads TDET{iwin}; the raw `TDET1` key names window 1 for every window. For stacks, read `sequence[0].meta.detector_band` before `stack_spectrogram_sequence` turns the meta into a plain dict (stack_spectrograms.py:80). Done when:
  - on local 3610108077, layers default to irissjiFUV for C II and Si IV, and to irissjiNUV for Mg II k and 2832 (`preferred_cmap` is None today);
  - the same holds for a 2-scan 4000005156 stack;
  - such a layer restores from a session.

  Features: F059. Depends: wp3-style-cmap.
- [ ] **M1** `wp11-physical-aspect`: Give raster maps physical pixel aspect with a glue-solar `viewer_tool` `solar:physical_aspect`, registered in `setup()` so restored viewers get it too.
  - It wraps the instance's private `state._set_axes_aspect_ratio` and multiplies the ratio by (arcsec per displayed x pixel)/(arcsec per y pixel), both measured as angular separations at the cube centre.
  - The factor is 1 unless both displayed axes are helioprojective with non-zero steps. Sit-and-stare, λ and time planes are therefore unchanged.
  - It calls `viewer._on_resize()` on `x_att`/`y_att`/`reference_data` changes, and the preset sets `aspect='equal'` on maps.
  - A probe switches it on when the aspect choices include no 'Physical pixels', and it has a `wp0-workaround-register` row (D2).
  - Upstream, on the user's direction: propose a glue-core `ImageViewerState.aspect` choice 'Physical pixels' that scales the ratio `_adjust_limits_aspect` uses (glue/viewers/matplotlib/state.py:182-250@1.27.0).

  Done when, on released core:
  - (a) local 4000005156 (about 12:1) and local 3400109360 (about 3:1) render a 10″×10″ solar square as square within 5%, at the preset size, after a resize and after a zoom;
  - (b) the dense 3610108077 raster looks unchanged, sit-and-stare stays readable, and a restored session re-installs the tool.

  Gated sub-check (c), closed with `wp0-release-tracking`: once a release contains the upstream choice, (a) and (b) pass with it and the probe switches the workaround off. Features: F193. Depends: wp4-quicklook-preset, wp10-m0-negative-step, wp0-workaround-register.
- [ ] **M1** `wp11-keyboard-shortcuts`: Register plain keys for `ImageViewer` and `ProfileViewer` through glue-qt's `keyboard_shortcut` registry (glue_qt/config.py:169@0.4.2):
  - D/F: previous/next frame on the axis that WP4 syncs (SJI frame, raster exposure/step, stack scan). D replaces CRISPEX's Shift+B, because B is glue's `image:contrast`.
  - A/S: previous/next wavelength (CRISPEX's Shift+A/S without Shift).
  - Space: toggle play/stop on the frame axis.

  Steps wrap. The callback receives only the session (application.py:498-522@0.4.2), so it finds the viewer through `session.application.current_tab.activeSubWindow().widget()`. In the quicklook, D/F move the WP4 master (so `wp4-time-sync` moves the followers), A/S move only the preset's wavelength index, and Space toggles `wp4-time-controls`. A Profile viewer acts on the master. Elsewhere, Space alternates the slice widget's `_adjust_play('forw')` and `_adjust_play('stop')` (data_slice_widget.py:146@0.4.2). Keys already registered for a viewer class are skipped. Name the keys in the tool tips and in the IRIS guide. Done when, on released glue-qt 0.4.2 with `QTest.keyClick`:
  - on a real SJI viewer and a real raster viewer, D/F step ±1 with wrap, and Space starts and stops playback;
  - after clicking the slice widget's forward and stop buttons (data_slice_widget.py:87-89) and after focusing its slider, Space toggles playback exactly once and D/F/A/S still step. If a focused button swallows Space, choose another free key and document it;
  - in the quicklook, D/F move the master and its synced partner, while A/S move only the wavelength index;
  - calling `setup()` twice raises nothing;
  - Tab and Backspace still cycle and close windows.

  Features: F197. Findings: followup-3-16, usefulness-17. Depends: wp4-quicklook-preset, wp4-time-sync, wp4-time-controls.

#### M2

- [ ] **M2** `wp11-colourbar`: Add a checkable glue-solar `viewer_tool` 'Colour bar' for Image viewers.

- **Retirement and private code.**

- **Readout cost and SJI coordinates.**
  - Every mouse move calls the raster WCS on the GUI thread. `wp10-m0-interaction-latency` bounds this cost and `wp10-m0-wcs-lock` makes it safe. Throttle the readouts only if they exceed the WP10 interaction budget.

  - glue-qt dispatch ignores modifiers.

issues.problem: The km formula is off by a factor of 1000. DSUN_OBS is in metres: the local 4000255147 SJI_1400 header has DSUN_OBS = 1.50921E+11, and irispy's `SGMeta.distance_to_sun` does `DSUN_OBS * u.m`. So arcsec × DSUN_OBS × π/648000 gives metres. Because the done_when says 'km within 0.1% of the formula', a value 1000× too large would pass.
issues.fix: Write the formula as km = arcsec × (π/648000) × DSUN_OBS[m] / 1000, or use (sep × DSUN_OBS·u.m).to(u.km) with sep in radians. Keep the done_when tied to that corrected formula and add an absolute check: 100 px × 0.16635″ at 1.509e11 m ≈ 12,170 km within 0.1%.

issues.problem: The critic issue is only partly applied. It asked to 'verify Space is not consumed by focused buttons, or choose another key', but the done_when sends keys only to the canvas. In glue-qt 0.4.2, `GlueApplication.keyPressEvent` (application.py:498-522) only sees keys that the focused widget does not consume. A focused QPushButton or QComboBox (for example in the slice widget or the layer options) takes Space, and focused list/tree widgets take letter keys.
issues.fix: Add to the done_when: after clicking the slice widget's forward/stop buttons (data_slice_widget.py:85-91@0.4.2) and after focusing its slider, Space toggles playback exactly once and D/F/A/S still step. If a focused button swallows Space, pick another play key and say so. Also note that the slice widget has separate 'forw' and 'stop' buttons, so describe the Space action as `_adjust_play('forw'/'stop')` toggling, not as pressing 'the play button'.

final.markdown:
### WP12: Export and derived diagrams

Goal: let users export what they see and derive, and add the derived diagrams CRISPEX offers: gap-aware time axes, x–t and spectral path diagrams, and multi-window light curves. Everything goes through glue registries: `viewer_tool` save subtools, `data_exporter`, D4 `layer_action`s, and core's released `BasePathSlicerMode`/`PathSlicedData` (glue-core 1.26.0 and later). Primary paths:
- `glue_solar/export.py`: sequence, profile, FITS and ECSV exporters.
- `glue_solar/paths.py`: path tools, path coordinates and the path saver.
- `glue_solar/sources/derived.py`: the time-regrid and light-curve actions.
- Registration in `glue_solar/__init__.py` `setup()`.
- Tests in `glue_solar/tests/test_export.py`, `test_paths.py` and `test_derived.py`.

What glue already offers: single-frame `mpl:save` and `save:python`, stock slider playback, and glue-qt 0.4.2's legacy 3D 'slice' (PV) tool. That tool gives an SJI x–t diagram with parent navigation, but it adds no Data, is disabled for 4D, and draft glue-qt #66 deletes it. Basic path drawing and 3D extraction are therefore not missing. What done means at each milestone:
- M1: the gap-aware time-axis Data (D7).
- M2: sequence and movie export, FITS export of derived products, point light curves, and 4D solar-coordinate path diagrams that save in sessions.
- M3: export annotations, profile-value export, overlays for saved paths, slope measurement, and batch re-extraction with nearest or linear sampling.

WP12 is the only home of movie, sequence and path work (plan-integrity-15). Each item brings its own data, units and lifecycle tests, not a new viewer framework.

**M1**

- [ ] **M1** `wp12-time-regrid`: Add a D4 `layer_action` 'Regrid on time' in `glue_solar/sources/derived.py`. This is D7's M1 time-axis adapter.
  - **Design (default, confirm).** The action adds a new regridded Data rather than using feas F142's in-place `_GlueWCS` step-as-time variant. This keeps the index Data unchanged and makes gaps visible.
  - **Inputs.** A sit-and-stare exposure axis, an SJI frame axis, or a 4D stack's scan axis at a fixed step. Choosing a scanning raster's step axis is refused.
  - **Grid.** The grid step is the median Δt of `Time`. Each pixel takes the nearest exposure within 0.75 × the median, otherwise NaN; one exposure may fill two pixels.
  - **Time.** A datetime64 `Time` component holds each pixel's source time (NaT in gaps). The WCS time world axis is 'Time since start', in seconds from DATEREF, so it does not collide with `Time`. WCSAxes shows seconds; UTC stays in `solar:frame_time`.
  - **Spatial axes.** They copy the middle matched exposure's calibration. The Data is therefore marked in `meta` and excluded from `link_hpc` (default, confirm), and the index Data stays the navigation source.

  Done when:
  - On 4000255147 Si IV (1600 exposures, cadence 2.71–3.29 s, median 2.89 s), the Data has ceil(span/2.89)+1 time pixels and 0 NaN columns, and each column equals its nearest exposure.
  - With 10 consecutive exposures removed, NaN columns appear only inside the gap.
  - The 4000255147 SJI 1400 (400 frames) and a stack of at least 4 scans of 3602506433 at a fixed step pass the same checks on their frame or scan axis.
  - WCSAxes labels the axis 'Time since start' (s).
  - Exactly one Data is added, no viewer opens, and `link_hpc` adds no link to the Data.
  - Choosing the step axis of 4000005156 scan 0 is refused with a message.
  - The Data survives a WP3 session round trip, rebuilt from the source label, axis, fixed index and grid stored in `meta`.

  Features: F089, F090. Findings: plan-integrity-7. Depends: `wp3-wcs-saver` (session rebuild).

**M2**

- [ ] **M2** `wp12-sequence-export`: Add a `viewer_tool` `solar:save_sequence` in `glue_solar/export.py`. In `setup()`, run `ImageViewer.subtools = deepcopy(ImageViewer.subtools)` and append the tool to 'save' (the `glue/plugins/tools/__init__.py` pattern).
  - **Range.** The tool asks for a slice axis (time, scan or exposure, or wavelength for a line scan) and an index range, prefilled from the `wp4-time-controls` range, then steps that viewer's slider.
  - **Whole-window mode.** The viewer becomes the D7 master for the run. NO MATCH partners are exported greyed, as displayed.
  - **Frames.** Per-frame PNG/JPEG comes from `figure.savefig` (viewer only, with an axes-off option through `ax.set_axis_off()` until glue #2128 is released) or from `GlueApplication.screenshot()` (whole window).
  - **Movies.** `matplotlib.animation` writes an `FFMpegWriter` MP4 when ffmpeg is on PATH, otherwise a `PillowWriter` GIF.
  - **Run.** Colour limits are frozen for the run. A `QProgressDialog` Cancel is checked between frames. Slice, master and axes are restored afterwards.

  Done when an offscreen pytest on 4000255147 SJI_1400 shows:
  - Frames 0–9 give 10 PNGs with identical colour limits, and frame i equals `mpl:save` at slice i.
  - Whole-window mode writes 10 window-size PNGs and restores the previous master.
  - A 20-index wavelength scan on a 4000005156 raster map writes 20 PNGs.
  - The GIF has 10 frames (PIL `n_frames`). The MP4 has 10 frames when ffmpeg is present; the check is skipped otherwise.
  - Cancel after 3 frames keeps and labels the partial output and restores the slider.
  - `MatplotlibDataViewer.subtools['save'] == ['mpl:save']`, and neither the Scatter nor the Histogram 'save' list contains `solar:save_sequence`.

  Features: F178, F179. Findings: core-qt-capabilities-9. Depends: `wp4-time-sync`, `wp10-m0-interaction-latency`, `wp4-time-controls` (range prefill only).

- [ ] **M2** `wp12-derived-data-export`: Register a `data_exporter` 'FITS (IRIS WCS + Time)' in `glue_solar/export.py`. The stock writers lose the WCS and `Time` (see Notes).
  - **Accepted data.** Only Data whose coords are `_GlueWCS` wrapping an astropy `WCS`. Anything else (gWCS SJI and AIA cubes, light curves, `PathSlicedData`, tables) is refused with a message naming the dataset.
  - **Contents.** Each numerical component becomes an ImageHDU with the raw WCS header (m and deg, as irispy stores them). A sliced map uses `raw.sub(<kept axes>)` plus a WAVELNTH or comment card for the fixed axis's world value. The file also holds the WCS-TABLE HDU for `-TAB` axes from WP3's `-TAB` record, the uint8 mask, and `Time` as MJD with TIMESYS='UTC'.
  - **Coverage.** WP2 moment maps, WP6 fit maps, the WP5 Doppler image, sliced raster maps, and wrapped File→Open sunpy maps. This is not the IRIS/CRISPEX Level-3 format, which stays a permanent non-goal.

  Done when, on 4000005156 Si IV scan 0, its WP2 moments map and a sliced raster map:
  - `WCS(header, fobj=hdul)` reproduces glue's world coordinates at 5 pixels within 1e-6 arcsec/Å, after unit conversion and ±180° wrapping (`glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:58-60`).
  - The sliced map's header records its fixed wavelength.
  - `Time` round-trips within 1 ms, and the mask HDU equals the mask.
  - A WP6 fit map exports all its parameter components.
  - `sunpy.map.Map` opens the export of a sunpy map.
  - Exporting an SJI or a WP12 light curve raises the message.

  Features: F182, F187. Findings: followup-3-8. Depends: `wp3-wcs-saver` (`-TAB` record), `wp2-m2-moment-maps`, `wp6-m2-fit-maps`, `wp5-m1-doppler-image`, `wp1-m1-sunpy-maps` (sunpy-map case only).

- [ ] **M2** `wp12-point-light-curves`: Add a D4 `layer_action` 'Light curves at this point' on a Pixel subset, in `glue_solar/sources/derived.py`. It refines old row 488, where `Time` is not a Profile x choice.
  - **Curves.** The action adds one 1D Data per chosen raster window (at a wavelength index, or `nanmean` over ±N) and per SJI or AIA channel. Each holds a datetime64 `Time` and the value, optionally mean-normalised.
  - **Links.** `LinkSame` links each curve's `Time` and value to the first curve's. Without these links, ScatterLayerArtist disables the other layers in a shared viewer.
  - **Display.** The action opens no viewer. The user or the WP4 preset adds the curves to one Scatter viewer, where WP7's `solar:time_marker` marks the master time.
  - **SJI sampling.** SJI frame t samples the raster point's world position at the exposure that the WP4 coordinator matched to t, through the per-frame SJI WCS, with no link-graph time resolution (D8). NO MATCH frames are NaN.
  - **Subset.** The Pixel subset stays bare and is never ANDed with a band subset (core-qt-capabilities-2).
  - **Updates.** The D9 coordinator recomputes the curves on the subset's `SubsetUpdateMessage`. After a session restore it re-attaches from the source labels, window, index or band, and normalisation stored in each curve's `meta`.
  - **Export.** Register a `data_exporter` 'ECSV (with Time)' in `glue_solar/export.py` for 1D Data with a datetime64 component, writing `Time` as ISO UTC (.cint parity).

  Done when, on 4000255147 with a point at slit pixel y:
  - Curves exist for Mg II k (at the index nearest the line-list 2796.35 Å), the C II core, and SJI 1400.
  - The raster curves equal `cube_w[:, y, k]` (1600 samples), and the band variant equals `nanmean(cube_w[:, y, k-N:k+N+1], -1)`.
  - The SJI curve has 400 samples equal to `sji[t, row(t), col(t)]`, with NaN at NO MATCH frames.
  - Mean-normalised curves average 1.
  - All curve layers are enabled in one Scatter viewer, and date ticks read 2013-09-02.
  - Dragging the point updates every curve, and the marker follows the master frame, also after a WP3 session round trip.
  - The Mg II k and SJI 1400 curves export to ECSV and re-read with `Time` equal within 1 ms.
  - `wp1-m0-link-graph-regression` passes with the curve links present.

  Features: F140, F141. Findings: core-qt-capabilities-2, plan-integrity-7. Depends: `wp4-time-sync`, `wp1-m0-link-hpc`, `wp10-fill-nan`, `wp7-goes-marker` (`solar:time_marker`), `wp7-goes-date-labels` (#2599 or its gated workaround), `wp3-coordination-reattach`, `wp7-aia-context` (AIA curves only).

- [ ] **M2** `wp12-path-slicer`: Build 4D, solar-coordinate path diagrams on core's released path slicer, not on the legacy glue-qt PV widget. Raise glue-solar's `glue-core>=1.23.0` floor to `>=1.26`, unless WP0 has already moved it to 1.27.0.
  - **Tool.** In `glue_solar/paths.py`, `solar:path` subclasses `BasePathSlicerMode`. It sets its own `tool_id` and `slice_viewer_cls`, the action_text 'Solar path (3D/4D)' and the shortcut 'L'. The inherited 'P'/'Slice Extraction' would clash with glue-qt 0.4.2's 'slice' tool, and 'L' is not among WP11's keys.
  - **Registration.** `setup()` appends `solar:path` and `solar:path_crosshair` to a copy of `ImageViewer.tools`.

The vertices are converted into that layer's pixel frame through world coordinates at the WP4 master frame, and the layer's own pixel components are used. It reuses core's `link_path_sliced_to_parent`, `link_path_sliced_pair_paths` and `open_slice_viewer_for`. Each product stores its drawn and reference-frame vertices in `meta['solar_path']`.

It overrides `activate` to draw the reference-frame vertices, and `_on_move` to move only the parent axis that the result's y axis represents. For a non-reference layer's product, it maps that axis through the WP4 coordinator's nearest-exposure arrays (D8), not by index equality.

**Notes and limits**

- **Pointing.** Path vertices, SJI traces and SJI light-curve positions use the WP4 master frame or matched exposure. A fixed pixel path does not follow pointing drift (D1). The regridded Data copies one exposure's calibration and stays out of `link_hpc`. Stack paths and arcsec distances use the scan-0 WCS until `wp1-stack-per-scan-wcs` (M3).
- **Stock exporters.** glue-core's gridded FITS writer writes a header only for an astropy `WCS` (`gridded_fits.py:52`@1.27.0) and skips the datetime64 `Time`. The HDF5, FITS-table and VOTable exporters raise 'No conversion path for dtype <M8[ns]'. That is why WP12 has its own FITS and ECSV exporters. Core's default path sampling truncates, so it is biased by up to 1 px; 'nearest' removes the bias.
- **sunpy and `-TAB`.** Raster-derived exports keep irispy's `HPLT-TAB`/`HPLN-TAB` axes. astropy therefore needs the HDUList: `WCS(header)` alone raises "HDUList is required to retrieve -TAB coordinates" (checked 2026-09-27 on irispy 0.9.0). `sunpy.map.Map` cannot open these exports. A linearised TAN header for sunpy is not planned; add one only on request.
- **Not rebuilt.**
  - CRISPEX's phi-slit angle/length sliders are covered by an arbitrary polyline.
  - Path width (averaging across a path) is dropped, because no in-scope feature asks for it.
  - IDL SAVE formats: .csav/.clsav/.cint/.cses are replaced by FITS, ECSV and glue sessions.
  - Level-3 FITS writing and EIS stay permanent non-goals.
- **Until M2.** For a 3D SJI, the documented x–t workflow is glue-qt 0.4.2's 'slice' tool (WP9), and `mpl:save` covers single frames. MP4 export will need ffmpeg on PATH, which is not a dependency; the GIF fallback uses Pillow, which matplotlib already installs.
- **Upstream (WP0).**
  - Report the datetime64 exporter failure.
  - Register the private hooks WP12 overrides: path tool `_on_reference_data_change`, `_open_or_update` and `_refresh_overlays`; crosshair `activate` and `_on_move`; `PathSlicedData._get_pix_coords`/`get_data`. List them with the upstream offers that would remove them: a `PathSlicedData` saver, the 4D gate, per-layer conversion and per-axis parent driving, and sampling modes.
  - Track glue #2128 (hide axes), #2599 (Scatter dates) and glue-qt #66 (`wp0-track-qt66`).
  - glue-qt #75 (ISO labels on WCS time sliders) improves the slider side of the time axis, but no WP12 done-when needs it.

issues.problem: This rests on a misreading of core, which the critic issue also made. `Tool.close()` runs only from the viewer's `window_closed` signal (glue/viewers/common/tool.py:35,50-56@1.27.0). When `BasePathSlicerMode.close()` removes the overlays (matplotlib_mode.py:122-127), the viewer is already closing. Deactivating the mode never removes them. So 'keep overlays after the tool closes' is meaningless and the done-when cannot be tested. The real F127 gap is different. `_traces` (multi_trace.py) belongs to each tool instance and is not restored. After a session restore, or after 'Load path', saved paths are therefore not drawn on the parent at all.

issues.problem: Both named functions are module-level functions, not methods, so a subclass cannot override them. `create_trace` is called from `MultiTracePathSlicerMixin._open_or_update` (multi_trace.py:56-72). `drive_parent_slice` is called only by `BasePathSlicerCrosshairMode._on_move` (matplotlib_mode.py:195-207), which is a separate tool on the slice viewer and is not the path tool. The disposition core-qt-capabilities-3 names that crosshair mode, but the draft never mentions it. Per-layer vertex conversion also breaks two core drawing paths. `_refresh_overlays` draws `trace[0].x/y`, and the crosshair draws `data.x/y`, both on the parent axes. Once the vertices are converted per layer, a non-reference layer's product is not in the parent's pixel frame. Clicking an SJI trace's diagram at frame t also cannot write index t onto a raster-referenced parent.
issues.fix: Say that `solar:path` overrides `_on_reference_data_change` (3D/4D gate), `_open_or_update` (per-layer conversion) and `_refresh_overlays` (draw the reference-frame vertices stored with the trace). Add a second viewer_tool, `solar:path_crosshair`, subclassing `BasePathSlicerCrosshairMode`, whose `_on_move` drives only the represented parent axis. For a non-reference layer, it maps the product's axis through the WP4 coordinator's time matching (D8), not by index equality. Add a done-when: 'clicking frame t in the SJI trace's diagram moves the raster viewer to the WP4-matched exposure'.

The 'vertices' test would then compare samples, not vertices.

issues.fix: Name the format and what it must contain, for example: ''Export data values' as FITS writes every numerical component; HDF5 is expected to raise until the upstream datetime64 fix (WP0)'. Or route the diagram through a WP12 exporter that writes `Time` as MJD.

issues.problem: The F140/F141 light curves that CRISPEX saves as .cint are Scatter-viewer 1D Data carrying a datetime64 `Time`. `solar:save_profile` covers only Profile-viewer layers. The stock exporters raise on datetime64, or drop it in FITS, so the WP12 light-curve product itself cannot be exported with its times.
issues.fix: Also register the ECSV writer as a `data_exporter` 'ECSV (with Time)' for 1D Data with a datetime64 component, so light-curve Data export with UTC. Add a done-when: 'the 4000255147 Mg II k and SJI 1400 curves export to ECSV and re-read with Time equal within 1 ms'.
